exports.name: BasinCollection
exports.doc:
Selected D8 drainage basins (possibly nested) on a ``FlowInfo`` topology.

Made by ``FlowInfo.basins(outlets)``. Basin ``basin_id`` (0-based) is the
whole upslope area of its outlet pixel; basins may nest (a basin whose
outlet lies inside another basin). Each basin is stored as a view of the
flow topology, so collections are cheap. ``table`` describes each basin,
``polygons`` gives outlines, ``labels`` and ``mask()`` give rasters, and
``statistics(dem)`` summarises elevation, slope and shape.

Returned by ``line_crossing_basins()``, ``FlowInfo.basins()``, ``SideTributaryBasins.basins``; not constructible directly.

Attributes
----------
labels : Raster
    Raster of basin membership: ``basin_id + 1``, 0 outside all basins.
polygons : geopandas.GeoDataFrame
    Basin outline polygons as a GeoDataFrame.
size : int
    Number of basins.
table : pandas.DataFrame
    One row per basin (pandas.DataFrame).

Methods
-------
mask(basin_id: int) -> Raster
    Return a 0/1 Raster of one basin.
membership(row: int, col: int) -> object
    Return all selected basin IDs containing this pixel.
outline_ridgelines(dem: Raster, split_method: str = 'longest_channel') -> object
    Split every selected basin outline into two ridgelines.
pixels(basin_id: int) -> object
    Return the pixels of one basin.
statistics(dem: Raster, include_slope: bool = True, include_flow_distance: bool = True, include_shape_metrics: bool = False, perimeter_simplify_cells: float = 1.0, bearings_relative_to_true_north: bool = False) -> object
    Return per-basin elevation, slope, flow-distance, and optional shape statistics.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

members.doc:
Raster of basin membership: ``basin_id + 1``, 0 outside all basins.

Basins are painted in ``basin_id`` order, so a pixel inside several nested
basins carries the largest ``basin_id + 1`` among them. Nodata where the DEM
is nodata.

members.doc:
statistics(self, dem: lsdtt3.Raster, include_slope: bool = True, include_flow_distance: bool = True, include_shape_metrics: bool = False, perimeter_simplify_cells: float = 1.0, bearings_relative_to_true_north: bool = False) -> object

Return per-basin elevation, slope, flow-distance, and optional shape statistics.

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Elevation (m) on the flow grid.
include_slope : bool, default=True
    Add ``slope_25th``, ``slope_50th``, ``slope_75th``: percentiles of the
    3 x 3 gradient (m/m, as ``slope()``).
include_flow_distance : bool, default=True
    Add ``flow_distance_25th/50th/75th``: percentiles of D8 flow distance
    to the outlet (m).
include_shape_metrics : bool, default=False
    Add planform shape metrics: ``centroid_x``, ``centroid_y``,
    ``basin_length_metres``, ``elongation_ratio``, ``form_factor``,
    ``circularity_ratio``, ``gravelius_compactness``, ``solidity``,
    ``eccentricity``, ``orientation_degrees`` (principal axis, compass,
    0-180, from grid north unless ``bearings_relative_to_true_north``),
    ``hypsometric_integral``.
perimeter_simplify_cells : float, default=1.0
    Simplification tolerance of the outline, in cells, used for the
    perimeter in the shape metrics.
bearings_relative_to_true_north : bool, default=False
    Convert ``orientation_degrees`` to true north with the grid convergence
    at the basin centroid, as the CLI's ``bearings_relative_to_true_north``;
    needs a flow grid with a CRS. False keeps it relative to grid north.

Returns
-------
pandas.DataFrame
    One row per basin: ``basin_id``, ``n_pixels``, ``area_metres2``,
    ``elevation_min``, ``elevation_max``, ``elevation_mean``,
    ``elevation_median``, ``elevation_stddev`` (m), plus the optional
    columns above.

One row per basin (pandas.DataFrame).

Columns: ``basin_id`` (0-based), ``outlet_flat``, ``outlet_row``,
``outlet_col``, ``n_pixels``, ``area_metres2`` (m^2), ``complete`` (False if

-1 if none), ``nesting_depth`` (0 for a basin with no parent).

exports.name: CRNColumn
exports.doc:
One-dimensional cosmogenic-nuclide column model.

Set an erosion history, ordered from present backwards in time, then use
``transient`` to model depth profiles. Point steady-state and step-change
calculations require no history. Erosion rates for these point calculations
are effective rates in g/cm²/yr.

The history (``set_erosion_history`` or ``read_erosion_history``) has rows
``time`` (years before present at which the rate changes, increasing),
``rate`` (erosion rate in m/yr; 0 means an instantaneous removal event) and
``removal`` (metres removed, used only when rate is 0); the last row must be
``time = -9999`` with the positive long-term background rate.

Construct it as

    CRNColumn(rock_density_kg_m3: float = 2650.0)

Parameters
----------
rock_density_kg_m3 : float, default=2650.0
    Rock density (kg/m^3, positive) converting depths in m to effective
    depths in g/cm^2 (``depth_m * density * 0.1``).

Attributes
----------
depth_change_m : float
    Total depth (m) removed over the history: added to sampling depths to get their starting depths.
erosion_rate_m_yr : list[float]
    History erosion rates (m/yr).
removal_m : list[float]
    History removal depths (m).
rock_density_kg_m3 : float
    Rock density (kg/m^3).
time_yr_bp : list[float]
    History times (years before present).

Methods
-------
read_erosion_history(path: str) -> None
    Read the erosion history from a CSV file with header ``time,rate,removal``.
set_erosion_history(time_yr_bp: Sequence[float], erosion_rate_m_yr: Sequence[float], removal_metres: Sequence[float]) -> None
    Set the history. Last row must be ``time=-9999`` with a positive background rate.
steady_state(effective_depth_g_cm2: float = 0.0, effective_erosion_rate_g_cm2_yr: float = 0.01, production_scaling: float = 1.0, total_shielding: float = 1.0, muon_scheme: str = 'BraucherBorchers') -> CRNColumnSample
    Return steady-state concentrations at one effective depth.
step_change(effective_depth_g_cm2: float = 0.0, effective_erosion_rate_old_g_cm2_yr: float = 0.01, effective_erosion_rate_new_g_cm2_yr: float = 0.01, time_since_step_yr: float = 0.0, production_scaling: float = 1.0, total_shielding: float = 1.0, muon_scheme: str = 'BraucherBorchers') -> CRNColumnSample
    Return concentrations after a step change in erosion rate.
transient(sampling_depths_metres: Sequence[float], production_scaling: float = 1.0, total_shielding: float = 1.0, muon_scheme: str = 'BraucherBorchers', initial_10be: float = -1.0, initial_26al: float = -1.0, initial_14c: float = -1.0) -> list[CRNColumnSample]
    Run the erosion history and return concentrations at the given depths.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

Returned by ``extract_channel_heads()``; not constructible directly.

exports.name: ChannelNetwork
exports.doc:
A D8 channel network as a graph of junctions and links.

Made by ``FlowInfo.channel_network(scope)``: every resolved source of the
``ChannelScope`` is traced downstream to its D8 outlet (outlet truncation in
the scope does not cut the network). A junction is a source, a confluence or
an outlet pixel; a link is the channel between a junction and the next
junction downstream. Stream orders are Strahler orders. Use
``lines_geodataframe()`` / ``points_geodataframe()`` for GIS layers,
``channel_mask`` as the ``channels`` raster of HAND, and ``chi()`` for chi
analysis.

Returned by ``FlowInfo.channel_network()``, ``DivideMigrationResult.network``; not constructible directly.

Attributes
----------
channel_mask : Raster
    0/1 Raster: 1 on network channel pixels, 0 on other valid pixels.
junction_id : numpy.ndarray
    Int32 array (n_rows, n_cols) of the junction ID at junction pixels, -1 elsewhere.
n_channel_cells : int
    Number of channel pixels in the network.
n_junctions : int
    Number of junctions (sources, confluences and outlets).

Methods
-------
basin_com_bearings(bearings_relative_to_true_north: bool = False) -> object
    Return outlet-to-basin-centre-of-mass bearings for each junction basin.
chi(outlets: object | None = None, m_over_n: float = 0.45, reference_area: float = 1.0, denominator: object | None = None) -> ChiCollection
    Extract outlet-seeded chi coordinates on this channel network.
chi_sweep(dem: Raster, m_over_n_values: object, outlets: object | None = None, reference_area: float = 1.0, critical_divergence_metres: float = 5.0, denominator: object | None = None) -> object
    Fit each tested m/n and return per-basin disorder.
donors(junction_id: int) -> list[int]
    Return the IDs of the junctions that drain directly into a junction.
junction_angles(junctions: object | None = None, mode: str = 'full_link', fixed_length_metres: float = 0.0, fixed_n_pixels: int = 0, min_nodes: int = 2) -> object
    Measure two-donor confluence angles in compass degrees.
junctions() -> object
    Return junction topology as a pandas DataFrame.
junctions_geodataframe() -> object
    Return channel junctions as a GeoPandas point layer.
lines_geodataframe() -> object
    Return compact non-outlet channel links as a GeoPandas line layer.
link_bearings(junctions: object | None = None, mode: str = 'full_link', fixed_length_metres: float = 0.0, fixed_n_pixels: int = 0, anchor: str = 'upstream', min_nodes: int = 2, bearings_relative_to_true_north: bool = False) -> object
    Fit compass bearings to compact channel links.
link_profiles(values: Raster, junctions: object | None = None) -> object
    Sample a raster along compact downstream channel links.
links() -> object
    Return junction-to-junction links as a pandas DataFrame.
points_geodataframe() -> object
    Return channel pixels as a GeoPandas point layer.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

members.name: chi
members.doc:
chi(self, outlets: object | None = None, m_over_n: float = 0.45, reference_area: float = 1.0, denominator: object | None = None) -> lsdtt3.ChiCollection

Extract outlet-seeded chi coordinates on this channel network.

chi is the integral of ``(A0 / A)**m_over_n`` along the channel from the
outlet upstream (trapezoidal rule on D8 steps), so it has units of metres
and is 0 at each outlet. Plotting elevation against chi gives straight
lines where channel steepness is uniform.

Parameters
----------
outlets : array-like of int or None, default=None
    N x 2 array of ``(row, col)`` outlet pixels on the network, one basin
    each. None uses every outlet of the network.
m_over_n : float, default=0.45
    Concavity index theta = m/n (dimensionless, positive).
reference_area : float, default=1.0
    Reference drainage area A0 in m^2 (positive). With A0 = 1 m^2 the
    fitted chi-elevation slope equals the steepness index k_sn.
denominator : Raster or None, default=None
    Replacement for drainage area A in the integrand (for example a
    discharge raster, in the same units as A0); must be positive on the
    channels. None uses D8 drainage area (m^2).

Returns
-------
ChiCollection
    Chi values for each outlet's channel pixels.

exports.name: ChannelScope
exports.doc:
The set of channel pixels selected for analysis, and the source of each.

Made by ``FlowInfo.channel_scope`` (or ``FlowInfo.scope_from_heads``). The
mode depends on what was supplied: ``"all_channels_threshold"`` (no
sources: every pixel with at least the threshold contributing pixels),
``"user_sources"`` (each source traced downstream to its outlet) or
``"user_sources_bounded"`` (each traced channel stops at its matched
outlet). Pass it to ``FlowInfo.channel_network`` to build a junction graph.

Returned by ``FlowInfo.channel_scope()``, ``FlowInfo.scope_from_heads()``; not constructible directly.

Attributes
----------
mask : Raster
    0/1 Raster of in-scope channel pixels.
mode : str
    Scope mode: 'all_channels_threshold', 'user_sources' or 'user_sources_bounded'.
outlets : numpy.ndarray
    Per resolved source, the (row, col) where its channel is cut, or (-1, -1) if it runs to the DEM outlet.
source_id : numpy.ndarray
    Int32 array (n_rows, n_cols): index of the source that first claims each channel pixel, -1 elsewhere.
sources : numpy.ndarray
    Resolved (snapped) source pixels as an N x 2 int64 (row, col) array; unsnappable inputs are dropped.

Methods
-------

exports.name: ChiCollection
exports.doc:
Chi coordinates of the channel pixels of one or more basins.

Made by ``ChannelNetwork.chi()``. Basin ``basin_id`` (0-based) is the
``basin_id``-th outlet. Chi (m) is 0 at each outlet and increases upstream.
``nodes()`` gives the values as a table, ``raster()`` as a Raster, and
``fit(dem)`` fits piecewise-linear segments in chi-elevation space to give
channel steepness (k_sn).

Returned by ``ChannelNetwork.chi()``, ``DivideMigrationResult.chi``; not constructible directly.

Attributes
----------
n_basins : int
    Number of basins (outlets).

Methods
-------
fit(dem: Raster, critical_divergence_metres: float = 5.0, mainstem: str = 'max_flow_length') -> ChiFit
    Fit piecewise-linear channel profiles in chi-elevation space.
nodes() -> object
    Return extracted channel chi nodes as a pandas DataFrame.
raster() -> Raster
    Return chi values as a masked Raster.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

members.name: fit
members.doc:
fit(self, dem: lsdtt3.Raster, critical_divergence_metres: float = 5.0, mainstem: str = 'max_flow_length') -> lsdtt3.ChiFit

Fit piecewise-linear channel profiles in chi-elevation space.

Each basin's main stem and then each tributary is fitted with straight
segments between its ends; a segment is split at its worst-fitting pixel
while the elevation misfit there exceeds ``critical_divergence_metres``.
Each segment's slope dz/dchi is its k_sn.

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Elevation (m) on the network grid, normally the conditioned DEM.
critical_divergence_metres : float, default=5.0
    Largest allowed vertical misfit (m) between the observed profile and a
    segment before the segment is split (non-negative). Larger values give
    fewer, longer segments; noisier DEMs need larger values (for example
    10 m on a 30 m DEM).
mainstem : {"max_flow_length", "max_chi"}, default="max_flow_length"
    How the main stem of each basin is chosen: the longest D8 flow path,
    or the path reaching the largest chi.

Returns
-------
ChiFit
    Fitted nodes, segments and per-basin k_sn summaries.

signatures.definition: def fit(self, dem: lsdtt3.Raster, critical_divergence_metres: float = \0, mainstem: str = \1) -> lsdtt3.ChiFit

exports.name: ChiFit
exports.doc:
Piecewise-linear fits of channel profiles in chi-elevation space.

Made by ``ChiCollection.fit(dem)``. Each segment is a straight line in
(chi, elevation); its slope ``ksn = dz/dchi`` is the channel steepness
index. With ``reference_area = 1`` m^2 this is k_sn in m^(2 theta), where
theta = m_over_n; with another A0 it is k_sn / A0**theta (dimensionless).
All three tables are pandas DataFrames; ``basin_id`` is 0-based and
``flat`` values are flat indices (row = flat // n_cols, col = flat % n_cols;
or ``FlowInfo.row_col(flat)``). lsdviztools3 chi plots expect the column
names ``basin_index`` and ``k_sn``: rename with
``df.rename(columns={"basin_id": "basin_index", "ksn": "k_sn"})``.

Returned by ``ChiCollection.fit()``; not constructible directly.

Attributes
----------
nodes : pandas.DataFrame
    One row per channel pixel: ``basin_id``, ``outlet_flat``, ``flat``,
    ``receiver_flat``, ``chi`` (m), ``observed_elevation`` (m),
    ``fitted_elevation`` (m), ``residual_elevation`` (observed - fitted, m),
    ``abs_residual_elevation`` (m), ``branch_id``, ``is_main_stem``,
    ``is_source``, ``is_junction``, ``is_split_point`` (pixel where segments
    meet), ``source_key`` (the chi data maps' channel key; -1 in a basin whose
    upslope area touches nodata). There are no row/col columns: use ``flat``
    as above.
segments : pandas.DataFrame
    One row per segment: ``basin_id``, ``outlet_flat``, ``segment_id``,
    ``parent_segment_id``, ``branch_id``, ``downstream_flat``,
    ``upstream_flat``, ``downstream_chi``, ``upstream_chi`` (m),
    ``downstream_elevation``, ``upstream_elevation`` (m), ``ksn``,
    ``max_abs_residual`` (m), ``n_nodes``, ``source_key``.
tributaries : pandas.DataFrame
    One row per tributary (a branch of the fit, head to the node where it
    joins its parent; branch 0 is the main stem), as lsdtt-chi-analysis
    ``write_chi_tributary_table``: ``basin_id``, ``basin_key``, ``source_key``,
    ``branch_id``, ``parent_branch_id``, ``branch_order``, ``head_flat``,
    ``junction_flat``, ``head_x``, ``head_y``, ``junction_x``, ``junction_y``,
    ``junction_drainage_area_m2`` (just before the junction),
    ``basin_drainage_area_m2``, ``area_fraction``, ``area_rank_in_basin``
    (1 = largest tributary), ``length_m``, ``chi_span``, ``n_segments``,
    ``ksn_min``, ``ksn_median``, ``ksn_max``, ``ksn_max_segment_id``,
    ``ksn_max_chi``, ``n_descendants``.
knickpoints : pandas.DataFrame
    One row per node where two fitted segments meet, as lsdtt-chi-analysis
    ``write_chi_knickpoint_table``: ``basin_id``, ``basin_key``, ``source_key``,
    ``branch_id``, ``upstream_segment_id``, ``downstream_segment_id``,
    ``flat``, ``x``, ``y``, ``chi``, ``elevation``, ``flow_distance_m``,
    ``drainage_area_m2``, ``ksn_upstream``, ``ksn_downstream``, ``delta_ksn``
    (upstream minus downstream), ``log_ratio_ksn``, ``at_junction`` (1 at a
    tributary mouth), ``chi_from_branch_head``, ``chi_normalised``.
knickpoint_thresholds : pandas.DataFrame
    Suggested thresholds for a major knickpoint, over the rows with
    ``at_junction`` 0: ``measure`` (``abs_delta_ksn``,
    ``abs_log_ratio_ksn``, ``ksn``), ``method`` (``p90``, ``p95``,
    ``median_plus_3mad``, ``otsu``; ``q3_plus_3iqr`` for ``ksn``),
    ``threshold``, ``n_above``, ``n_total``.
summary : pandas.DataFrame
    One row per basin: ``basin_id``, ``outlet_flat``, ``n_segments``,
    ``n_main_stem_segments``, ``total_chi_length`` (m), ``mean_ksn``,
    ``median_ksn``, ``min_ksn``, ``max_ksn``, ``chi_weighted_mean_ksn``,
    ``main_stem_mean_ksn``, ``main_stem_median_ksn``.

Methods
-------

    Return full-network chi-disorder per basin.

    Bootstrap disorder over side branches.

    Leave-one-side-branch-out disorder samples.

    Evaluate disorder across mainstem-plus-tributary subsets.

    Run regularised spatial ksn/u-star inversion over m/n trials.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

invert_ksn(self, m_over_n_values: object, reference_area: float = 1.0, coarse_cell_size_metres: float = 2000.0, roughness_weight: float = 10000.0, diagonal_jitter: float = 1e-08, use_mae: bool = True) -> lsdtt3.ChiInversion

Run regularised spatial ksn/u-star inversion over m/n trials.

For each tested m/n, solves on a coarse grid for the regularised field of
u-star (normalised uplift) that best reproduces the channel elevations, and
selects the m/n with the lowest misfit.

Parameters
----------
m_over_n_values : array-like of float
    Concavity values to test (non-empty).
reference_area : float, default=1.0
    Reference drainage area A0 (m^2) used for chi.
coarse_cell_size_metres : float, default=2000.0
    Cell size (m) of the coarse grid on which u-star is solved.
roughness_weight : float, default=1e4
    Weight of the roughness (smoothness) regularisation term.
diagonal_jitter : float, default=1e-8
    Small value added to the normal-equation diagonal for numerical
    stability.
use_mae : bool, default=True
    Select the best m/n by mean absolute error (True) or RMSE (False).

Returns
-------
ChiInversion
    Trial, summary and node tables, and u-star rasters.

exports.name: FlowGraph
exports.doc:
Fractional D-infinity or MFD flow-routing graph.

Use ``FlowInfo`` for single-receiver D8 channel trees. Use ``FlowGraph`` for
distributed-flow drainage area and later TWI/connectivity calculations.

Construct it as

    FlowGraph(dem: Raster, method: str = 'mfd', boundary_conditions: str = 'oooo', interior_nodata_is_outlet: bool = True, mfd_exponent: float = 1.0, n_threads: int = 0)

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Depression-conditioned elevation raster (m).
method : {"mfd", "dinf"}, default="mfd"
    ``mfd``: flow split among all downslope neighbours weighted by
    slope**mfd_exponent (Quinn et al. 1991; Freeman 1991). ``dinf``:
    D-infinity (Tarboton 1997), flow split between the two neighbours of
    the steepest triangular facet.
boundary_conditions : str, default='oooo'
    Four NESW edge codes, as for ``FlowInfo``.
interior_nodata_is_outlet : bool, default=True
    Pixels next to nodata may drain into it.
mfd_exponent : float, default=1.0
    Exponent on slope in the MFD split (1.0 Quinn, 1.1 Freeman).
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.

Attributes
----------
donor_count : numpy.ndarray
    Uint8 array: number of cells draining into each cell.
metadata : RasterMeta

n_valid_cells : int
outlets : numpy.ndarray
    Outlet pixels as an N x 2 (row, col) array.
shape : tuple
valid_mask : numpy.ndarray
    Bool array (n_rows, n_cols), True for valid pixels.

exports.name: FlowInfo
exports.doc:
D8 drainage topology (steepest-descent receivers) of a conditioned DEM.

Each valid pixel drains to the one of its eight neighbours with the steepest
downhill gradient, or is an outlet. ``FlowInfo`` stores this routing (and
each pixel's upslope pixels), not the elevations, so later calls that need
elevations take the DEM again. Fill or breach depressions first (for example
``fill_pits``); a pixel with no downhill neighbour and no allowed exit raises
an error unless ``allow_pits_as_outlets=True``. Pixels are addressed by
``(row, col)`` (row 0 is the northern edge) or by flat index
``row * n_cols + col``.

Typical workflow::

    F = lsdtt3.FlowInfo(lsdtt3.fill_pits(dem))
    scope = F.channel_scope(threshold_contributing_pixels=1000)
    N = F.channel_network(scope)
    B = F.basins(outlets, min_upslope_pixels=0)

Construct it as

    FlowInfo(dem: Raster, boundary_conditions: str = 'oooo', interior_nodata_is_outlet: bool = True, forced_outlets: object | None = None, allow_pits_as_outlets: bool = False, n_threads: int = 0)

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Depression-conditioned elevation raster (m) in a projected metre CRS.
boundary_conditions : str, default='oooo'
    Four characters for the north, east, south and west edges: ``o`` open
    (an edge pixel may drain out of the grid when it has no lower in-grid
    neighbour), ``n`` no-flux (flow cannot leave), ``p`` periodic (wraps to
    the opposite edge; must be given for both opposite edges), ``b``
    base level (every pixel on the edge is an outlet). See
    ``make_boundary_conditions``.
interior_nodata_is_outlet : bool, default=True
    If True, a pixel next to a nodata pixel may drain into it (become an
    outlet) when it has no lower valid neighbour, as at a coastline or the
    edge of a clipped DEM. If False such pixels must drain over valid pixels.
forced_outlets : array-like of int or None, default=None
    N x 2 array of ``(row, col)`` pixels that are made outlets regardless of
    their neighbours (moulins, swallow holes, playas). Prepare the DEM with
    ``fill_pits_with_sinks`` using the same pixels. Out-of-grid or nodata
    pixels raise ``ValueError``; duplicates are ignored.
allow_pits_as_outlets : bool, default=False
    If True, a pixel that has no downhill neighbour and no allowed exit
    becomes an outlet instead of raising an error (useful in landscape
    evolution runs where transient pits form).
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.

Attributes
----------
boundary_conditions : str
    The four-character NESW boundary-condition string used.
direction : numpy.ndarray
    Uint8 array (n_rows, n_cols) of internal D8 direction codes; see flow_direction() for a raster.
donor_count : numpy.ndarray
    Uint8 array (n_rows, n_cols): number of neighbours draining directly into each pixel.
metadata : RasterMeta
    Grid metadata (RasterMeta) of the DEM the topology was built from.
n_outlets : int
    Number of outlet pixels (pixels with no receiver).
n_valid_cells : int
    Number of valid (routed) pixels.
outlets : numpy.ndarray
    Outlet pixels as an N x 2 int64 array of (row, col), in flat-index order.
receiver : numpy.ndarray
    Int64 array (n_rows, n_cols) of each pixel's receiver flat index; -2 at outlets, -1 at nodata.
shape : tuple[int, int]
    Grid shape as (n_rows, n_cols).
valid_mask : numpy.ndarray
    Bool array (n_rows, n_cols), True for valid pixels.

Methods
-------
accumulate(weights: object | None = None) -> Raster
    Accumulate per-pixel weights downstream; default weights are cell areas.
basins(outlets: object | None = None, min_upslope_pixels: int = 0) -> BasinCollection
    Create a ``BasinCollection`` from explicit outlet pixels or all qualifying D8 outlets.
channel_mask(threshold_contributing_pixels: int) -> Raster
    Return a 0/1 raster where contributing pixels meet the threshold.
channel_network(scope: ChannelScope) -> ChannelNetwork
    Build a compact junction graph from a ChannelScope.
channel_point_attributes(filled_dem: Raster, points: geopandas.GeoDataFrame, *, threshold_contributing_pixels: int, slope_window_half_length_metres: float = 25.0, channel_points_snap_max_search_radius_pixels: int = 10) -> geopandas.GeoDataFrame
    Snap points (e.g. field sites) to the nearest channel cell and add its drainage area and along-channel slope.
channel_scope(threshold_contributing_pixels: int, sources: object | None = None, outlets: object | None = None, snap_sources: bool = True, source_snap_max_radius_pixels: int = 25, outlet_snap_max_distance_metres: float = 0.0, auto_detect_roles: bool = False, channel_definition_algorithm_choice: str = 'contributing_pixels', min_channel_stream_order: int = 3) -> ChannelScope
    Resolve threshold or supplied source paths into a ChannelScope.
chi_from_outlets(outlets: object | None = None, m_over_n: float = 0.45, reference_area: float = 1.0, denominator: object | None = None) -> Raster
    Integrate zero-based chi across complete upstream raster domains.
chi_from_outlets_inherited(outlets: object, seed_chi: Raster, m_over_n: float = 0.45, reference_area: float = 1.0, denominator: object | None = None) -> Raster
    Integrate chi from supplied outlets using seed-raster base values.
contributing_pixels() -> Raster
    Return the number of pixels draining through each pixel, including itself.
distance_to_channel(threshold_contributing_pixels: int) -> Raster
    Return the D8 flow-path length from each pixel to the nearest downstream channel.
distance_to_farthest_ridge() -> Raster
    Return the longest D8 flow-path length from any upslope pixel to this pixel.
downstream_sum(values: Raster, sinks: Raster) -> Raster
    Sum a raster along each pixel's D8 path down to the first sink pixel.
drainage_area() -> Raster
    Return the D8 drainage area of every pixel, including the pixel itself.
flat_index(row: int, col: int) -> int
    Return the flat index ``row * n_cols + col`` of a pixel.
flow_direction() -> Raster
    Return the D8 receiver direction of every pixel as a Raster of codes.
flow_distance_to_outlet() -> Raster
    Return the D8 flow-path length from each pixel to its outlet.
flow_lines_geodataframe() -> object
    Return all D8 receiver edges as a GeoPandas line layer.
height_above_channel(dem: Raster, channels: Raster) -> Raster
    Compute HAND (height above nearest drainage) from an explicit channel raster.
height_above_channel_with_donor(dem: Raster, channels: Raster) -> dict
    Compute HAND and the channel pixel ("donor") each pixel drains to.
height_to_farthest_ridge(dem: Raster) -> Raster
    Return the elevation difference to the farthest upslope ridge pixel.

    Return True if the pixel is an outlet (has no downstream receiver).

    Return True if the candidate pixel drains through the target pixel.

    Return the pixel this pixel drains to.
row_col(flat_index: int) -> tuple
    Return the ``(row, col)`` of a flat index.
scope_from_heads(heads: ChannelHeads, outlets: object | None = None, outlet_snap_max_distance_metres: float = 0.0) -> ChannelScope
    Resolve ChannelHeads into explicit D8 source paths for channel and chi analysis.
snap_points(x: object | None = None, y: object | None = None, *, longitude: object | None = None, latitude: object | None = None, points: object | None = None, crs: str | None = None, method: str = 'downstream', threshold_contributing_pixels: int | None = None, threshold_drainage_area_m2: float | None = None, min_search_radius_pixels: int = 0, max_search_radius_pixels: int = 25, max_search_radius_metres: float | None = None) -> object
    Snap points (for example basin outlets or sample sites) onto the flow network.
sources(threshold_contributing_pixels: int) -> object
    Return channel sources (channel heads) as an N by 2 (row, col) array.
upslope_mean(values: Raster, include_self: bool = True) -> Raster

    Sum a raster over the upslope area of every pixel.

members.name: channel_point_attributes
members.doc:
channel_point_attributes(self, filled_dem: Raster, points: geopandas.GeoDataFrame, *, threshold_contributing_pixels: int, slope_window_half_length_metres: float = 25.0, channel_points_snap_max_search_radius_pixels: int = 10) -> geopandas.GeoDataFrame

Snap points (e.g. field sites) to the nearest channel cell and add its drainage area and along-channel slope.

lsdtt-channel-extraction ``run_channel_point_attributes``, with the same
C++ routine and parameter names. Each point moves to the channel cell
(at least ``threshold_contributing_pixels`` contributing pixels) whose
centre is nearest in straight-line distance, within
``channel_points_snap_max_search_radius_pixels``; it does not follow the
D8 path. The slope is the least-squares slope of ``filled_dem`` against
distance along the channel over +/- ``slope_window_half_length_metres``;
upstream the window follows the largest-area tributary.

Parameters
----------
filled_dem : Raster
    The DEM this FlowInfo was built on (pit-filled); elevations and the
    slope are taken from it.
points : geopandas.GeoDataFrame
    Point geometries with a CRS (reprojected to the grid's). Every column
    is kept.
threshold_contributing_pixels : int, keyword-only
    Channel cells have at least this many contributing pixels; also the
    least a tributary must carry for the slope window to follow it.
slope_window_half_length_metres : float, default=25.0
    Half-length (m) of the along-channel slope window; at least two cell
    sizes.
channel_points_snap_max_search_radius_pixels : int, default=10
    Furthest a point may move, in pixels (Chebyshev rings).

Returns
-------
geopandas.GeoDataFrame
    ``points`` in the grid CRS with the geometry moved to the snapped cell
    centre, and the columns original_x, original_y (grid CRS),
    snap_distance_m, snap_status, snapped_flat, contributing_pixels,
    drainage_area_m2, flow_distance_m, elevation_m, smoothed_elevation_m,
    slope_m_per_m, slope_valid (0/1), slope_window_length_m. A point that
    does not snap keeps its position, with its snap_status and empty (NaN /
    <NA>) values. An added column whose name is already in ``points`` is
    renamed with the suffix ``_lsdtt`` (with a warning), as in the CLI.

--------
>>> filled = lsdtt3.fill_pits(dem)
>>> F = lsdtt3.FlowInfo(filled)
>>> sites = geopandas.read_file("field_sites.gpkg")

...                                  slope_window_half_length_metres=150.0)

members.name: channel_scope
members.doc:
channel_scope(self, threshold_contributing_pixels: int, sources: object | None = None, outlets: object | None = None, snap_sources: bool = True, source_snap_max_radius_pixels: int = 25, outlet_snap_max_distance_metres: float = 0.0, auto_detect_roles: bool = False, channel_definition_algorithm_choice: str = 'contributing_pixels', min_channel_stream_order: int = 3) -> lsdtt3.ChannelScope

Resolve threshold or supplied source paths into a ChannelScope.

With no ``sources``, every pixel whose contributing-pixel count reaches the
threshold is a channel. With ``sources``, only the channels traced
downstream from those points are used, optionally stopped at ``outlets``.

Parameters
----------
threshold_contributing_pixels : int
    Channel threshold: a pixel is a channel when the number of pixels
    draining through it (including itself) is >= this value; positive.
    Threshold area in m^2 is this times ``metadata.pixel_area`` (for
    example 1000 pixels on a 30 m grid is 0.9 km^2).
sources : array-like of int or None, default=None
    N x 2 array of ``(row, col)`` channel-head pixels (valid pixels). Each
    is traced downstream to its D8 outlet. None selects all channels.
outlets : array-like of int or None, default=None
    N x 2 array of ``(row, col)`` points where traced channels stop; needs
    ``sources``. Each outlet is matched to the nearest pixel on a traced
    path, and that path is cut there.
snap_sources : bool, default=True
    Move each source to the nearest pixel that meets the threshold
    (expanding-square search); sources that cannot be snapped are dropped.
    If False sources are used as given.
source_snap_max_radius_pixels : int, default=25
    Largest search radius, in pixels, for source snapping.
outlet_snap_max_distance_metres : float, default=0.0
    Largest distance (m) from an outlet point to the traced path it cuts;
    outlets farther away are ignored. 0 or negative means unlimited.
auto_detect_roles : bool, default=False
    Pass all points as ``sources`` and let roles be inferred: a point that
    lies downstream of another supplied point becomes an outlet that cuts
    that channel. Requires ``outlets=None``; sources are always snapped.
channel_definition_algorithm_choice : {"contributing_pixels", "stream_order"}, default="contributing_pixels"
    What counts as a channel pixel, as in lsdtt-fluvial-surfaces:
    ``contributing_pixels`` keeps every traced pixel; ``stream_order``
    keeps only traced pixels of Strahler order >= ``min_channel_stream_order``
    (Clubb et al. 2017 use 3). The threshold still decides which
    first-order channels exist, and so the order every pixel reaches.
min_channel_stream_order : int, default=3
    Lowest Strahler order kept under ``stream_order``.

Returns
-------
ChannelScope
    Selected channel pixels, resolved sources and outlets.

signatures.definition: def channel_scope(self, threshold_contributing_pixels: int, sources: object | None = \0, outlets: object | None = \1, snap_sources: bool = \2, source_snap_max_radius_pixels: int = \3, outlet_snap_max_distance_metres: float = \4, auto_detect_roles: bool = \5, channel_definition_algorithm_choice: str = \6, min_channel_stream_order: int = \7) -> lsdtt3.ChannelScope

members.name: snap_points
members.doc:
snap_points(self, x: object | None = None, y: object | None = None, *, longitude: object | None = None, latitude: object | None = None, points: object | None = None, crs: str | None = None, method: str = 'downstream', threshold_contributing_pixels: int | None = None, threshold_drainage_area_m2: float | None = None, min_search_radius_pixels: int = 0, max_search_radius_pixels: int = 25, max_search_radius_metres: float | None = None) -> object

Snap points (for example basin outlets or sample sites) onto the flow network.

Each point is placed in the pixel that contains it and then moved by
``method``. The result is the ``(row, col)`` array that
``FlowInfo.basins(outlets)``, ``ChannelNetwork.chi(outlets=...)`` and other
``outlets`` arguments take. Give the points as exactly one of ``x`` and
``y``, ``longitude`` and ``latitude``, or ``points``.

The methods, their names and their rules are those of the command-line
programs' ``basin_outlet_snapping_method`` (the same C++ routines): a
``method``, ``threshold_contributing_pixels`` and the two radii here give
the same pixel as ``basin_outlet_snapping_method``,
``basin_outlet_contributing_pixels_threshold`` and
``basin_outlet_snap_min/max_search_radius_pixels`` with the same values. A
pixel "qualifies" when its contributing-pixel count (the pixel itself and
all pixels draining through it) is at least the threshold (``>=``).

* ``"downstream"``: follow the D8 receivers from the point's pixel to the
  first qualifying pixel. The point must be on a valid pixel and upstream
  of a qualifying pixel. The radii are not used.
* ``"expanding_square"``: search square rings of half-width
  ``min_search_radius_pixels`` to ``max_search_radius_pixels`` around the
  point's pixel, one ring at a time, and take the nearest qualifying pixel
  (straight-line distance) in the first ring that has one; ties go to the
  larger drainage area, then the smaller flat index.
* ``"largest_area"``: the pixel with the largest drainage area in the
  square of half-width ``max_search_radius_pixels`` (ties: the nearer
  pixel, then the smaller flat index), provided it qualifies. This is the
  GIS "snap pour point" rule. With a wide square it can jump onto a bigger
  neighbouring river, so keep the square to a few pixels.
  ``min_search_radius_pixels`` is not used.

Error policy: if any point is outside the grid or cannot be snapped,
``ValueError`` is raised naming each such point (by its zero-based position
in the input) and the snapping status (``input_out_of_bounds``,
``input_invalid_flow_cell``, ``threshold_not_found_in_search_window`` or
``outlet_reached_before_threshold``); no partial result is returned.

Parameters
----------
x, y : float or array-like of float, optional
    Easting and northing of the points, in the flow grid's CRS
    (``F.metadata.crs_wkt``, metres) unless ``crs`` is given.
longitude, latitude : float or array-like of float, optional, keyword-only
    Point coordinates in decimal degrees, in ``crs`` (default WGS84,
    ``"EPSG:4326"``). Longitude is the x coordinate: pass both by keyword.
points : geopandas.GeoDataFrame or geopandas.GeoSeries, optional, keyword-only
    Point geometries with a CRS; they are transformed to the grid's CRS.
crs : str or None, default=None, keyword-only
    CRS of ``x``/``y`` or ``longitude``/``latitude`` as an ``"EPSG:<code>"``
    string, WKT or PROJ string. None means the grid's CRS for ``x``/``y`` and
    ``"EPSG:4326"`` for ``longitude``/``latitude``. Not used with ``points``.
method : {"downstream", "expanding_square", "largest_area"}, default="downstream", keyword-only
    Snapping rule, as described above.
threshold_contributing_pixels : int or None, default=None, keyword-only
    Contributing pixels (>= 1) a pixel needs to qualify; the CLIs'
    ``basin_outlet_contributing_pixels_threshold``. Give this or
    ``threshold_drainage_area_m2``, not both. With neither, every method
    uses that key's CLI default, 1000 contributing pixels (as a CLI run
    without the key does); pass ``threshold_contributing_pixels=1`` to
    ``"largest_area"`` for no minimum.
threshold_drainage_area_m2 : float or None, default=None, keyword-only
    The same threshold as a drainage area (m^2, > 0). It is converted to the
    smallest whole number of contributing pixels N with
    N * ``F.metadata.pixel_area`` >= ``threshold_drainage_area_m2``, so a
    pixel qualifies exactly when its drainage area (contributing pixels *
    pixel area) is >= ``threshold_drainage_area_m2``.
min_search_radius_pixels : int, default=0, keyword-only
    Smallest ring half-width (pixels, >= 0) for ``"expanding_square"``; 0
    tests the point's own pixel first. As
    ``basin_outlet_snap_min_search_radius_pixels``.
max_search_radius_pixels : int, default=25, keyword-only
    Largest ring half-width for ``"expanding_square"`` and the square's
    half-width for ``"largest_area"`` (pixels, >= 0). As
    ``basin_outlet_snap_max_search_radius_pixels``.
max_search_radius_metres : float or None, default=None, keyword-only
    ``max_search_radius_pixels`` in metres; if given it replaces it and is
    rounded up to whole pixels.

Returns
-------
numpy.ndarray
    N x 2 int64 array of snapped ``(row, col)`` pixels, one row per input
    point and in input order (row 0 is the north edge). Points may snap to
    the same pixel; ``FlowInfo.basins`` then keeps only the first.

Examples
--------
>>> F = lsdtt3.FlowInfo(lsdtt3.fill_pits(dem))
>>> outlets = F.snap_points(longitude=[15.79008, 16.06060], latitude=[37.94234, 38.06143],
...                         method="downstream", threshold_contributing_pixels=500)
>>> B = F.basins(outlets)

exports.name: JunctionBasinCollection
exports.doc:
Junction-aware D8 basins selected from a ``ChannelNetwork``.

Each basin drains to one channel junction and carries that junction's
Strahler stream order. The ``filter_*`` methods remove basins in place and
return the collection, so they can be chained:
``junction_basins(N).filter_incomplete().filter_stream_order(2, 2)``.
Created with :func:`junction_basins`.

Returned by ``junction_basins()``, ``JunctionBasinCollection.filter_area()``, ``JunctionBasinCollection.filter_incomplete()``, ``JunctionBasinCollection.filter_largest()`` and 3 more; not constructible directly.

----------

    Raster of each basin's junction ID; nested basins overwrite their parents; nodata outside all basins.

    One row per basin (pandas.DataFrame).

Methods
-------
filter_area(min_pixels: int = -1, max_pixels: int = -1) -> JunctionBasinCollection
    Keep basins whose pixel count is within [min_pixels, max_pixels].

    Remove basins that touch nodata or an open DEM edge; returns this collection.
filter_largest() -> JunctionBasinCollection
    Keep only the basin with the most pixels; returns this collection.

    Keep basins whose Strahler order is within [min_order, max_order].

exports.name: LandscapeModel
exports.doc:
Stateful coupled fluvial-incision and hillslope-transport landscape model.

The model owns its evolving elevation raster and reuses native hillslope solver
workspaces between calls to ``step`` or ``run``. Each step applies uplift,
stream-power fluvial incision ``E = K a**m S**n`` (``a = A / dx`` the
specific catchment area in m, ``S`` the gradient in m/m, ``E`` in m/yr) and
hillslope transport. Typical use::

    model = lsdtt3.LandscapeModel(dem, timestep_years=100, uplift_rate=1e-4)
    result = model.run(1000)          # 1000 steps of 100 years
    result.elevation.write("evolved.tif")

Construct it as

    LandscapeModel(dem: Raster, timestep_years: float = 100.0, erodibility: float = 0.001, m_exponent: float = 0.45, n_exponent: float = 1.0, uplift_rate: float = 0.0001, hillslope_diffusivity: float = 0.001, hillslope_model: str = 'cidre', nonlinear_hillslopes: bool = False, critical_hillslope_slope: float = 0.8, incision_threshold_specific_area: float = 0.0, coupling_regime: str = 'automatic', boundary_conditions: str = 'oooo', fluvial_method: str = 'd8', channel_mask: object | None = None, hold_channel_mask_fixed: bool = False, fixed_pixels: object | None = None, n_threads: int = 0, baselevel_fall_rate: float = 0.0, cellular_r_match: float = 0.85, cellular_cfl_safety: float = 0.8, cellular_nonlocal_fraction: float = 0.0, cellular_nonlocal_activation_ratio: float = 0.8, cellular_nonlocal_deposition_probability: float = 0.5, cellular_nonlocal_max_hops: int = 4, erodibility_field: object | None = None, erodibility_m_exponent: object | None = None, erodibility_area_convention: object | None = None)
    LandscapeModel(dem: Raster, timestep_years: float = 100.0, erodibility: float = 0.001, m_exponent: float = 0.45, n_exponent: float = 1.0, uplift_rate: float = 0.0001, hillslope_diffusivity: float = 0.001, hillslope_model: str = 'cidre', nonlinear_hillslopes: bool = False, critical_hillslope_slope: float = 0.8, incision_threshold_area: float = 0.0, coupling_regime: str = 'automatic', boundary_conditions: str = 'oooo', fluvial_method: str = 'd8', channel_mask: object | None = None, hold_channel_mask_fixed: bool = False, fixed_pixels: object | None = None, n_threads: int = 0, baselevel_fall_rate: float = 0.0, cellular_r_match: float = 0.85, cellular_cfl_safety: float = 0.8, cellular_nonlocal_fraction: float = 0.0, cellular_nonlocal_activation_ratio: float = 0.8, cellular_nonlocal_deposition_probability: float = 0.5, cellular_nonlocal_max_hops: int = 4, erodibility_field: object | None = None, erodibility_m_exponent: object | None = None, erodibility_area_convention: object | None = None)

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Initial, depression-conditioned elevation surface (m) in a projected
    metre CRS.
timestep_years : float, default=100.0
    Duration (years) of each call to ``step``.
erodibility : float, default=0.001
    Stream-power erodibility K (> 0), in the specific-area convention above;
    also the reference K for ``erodibility_field``.
m_exponent, n_exponent : float, default=0.45, 1.0
    Stream-power exponents on specific area and slope.
uplift_rate : float, default=0.0001
    Uniform rock uplift rate in m/yr.
hillslope_diffusivity : float, default=0.001
    Hillslope diffusivity D in m^2/yr.
hillslope_model : {"none", "linear", "roering", "roering_implicit", "cidre", "adi", "cellular"}, default="cidre"
    Hillslope process model: ``linear`` explicit diffusion, ``roering``
    explicit nonlinear flux (Roering et al. 1999), ``roering_implicit``
    backward-Euler nonlinear solver, ``cidre`` Carretier et al. (2016),
    ``adi`` implicit linear diffusion, ``cellular`` cellular transport;
    ``none`` disables hillslope transport.
nonlinear_hillslopes : bool, default=False
    Use the Roering nonlinear flux law where the model supports it.
critical_hillslope_slope : float, default=0.8
    Critical gradient S_c (m/m) of the nonlinear flux law.
incision_threshold_specific_area : float, default=0.0
    Channel threshold in specific catchment area A/dx (metres); zero supports fully coupled runs.
incision_threshold_area : float, default=0.0
    Deprecated alias of ``incision_threshold_specific_area`` (emits a
    ``DeprecationWarning``).
coupling_regime : {"automatic", "coupled", "channels_as_boundaries"}, default="automatic"
    ``coupled``: hillslope and fluvial processes act everywhere, so valleys
    and drainage density emerge; ``channels_as_boundaries``: channel pixels
    (above the threshold or in ``channel_mask``) are fixed boundaries of the
    hillslope solve; ``automatic`` chooses ``channels_as_boundaries`` when a
    positive threshold or a channel mask is given, else ``coupled``.
boundary_conditions : str, default='oooo'
    Four NESW codes: ``o`` open, ``n`` no-flux, ``p`` periodic, ``b`` base
    level.
fluvial_method : {"d8", "dinf", "none"}, default="d8"
    Fluvial incision routing method, or ``none`` for hillslope-only evolution.
channel_mask : Raster or None, default=None
    Same-grid 0/1 imposed channel raster.
hold_channel_mask_fixed : bool, default=False
    Add imposed channel pixels to the fixed-elevation set.
fixed_pixels : array-like of int or None, default=None
    Explicit N x 2 ``(row, col)`` fixed-elevation cells. None uses the open
    and base-level edges.
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; zero uses the runtime default.
baselevel_fall_rate : float, default=0.0
    Downward motion of fixed base-level cells in m/yr.
cellular_r_match : float, default=0.85
    ``cellular`` only: slope ratio r = S / S_c (0 < r < 1) above which the
    nonlinear mobility ``1 / (1 - r**2)`` is continued linearly, avoiding
    the singularity at S_c.
cellular_cfl_safety : float, default=0.8
    ``cellular`` only: stability safety factor on the substep (0 < f <= 1).
cellular_nonlocal_fraction : float, default=0.0
    ``cellular`` only: fraction of near-critical excess flux moved
    non-locally (0 keeps the local solver exactly).
cellular_nonlocal_activation_ratio : float, default=0.8
    ``cellular`` only: slope / S_c ratio (0-1) above which non-local
    transfer starts.
cellular_nonlocal_deposition_probability : float, default=0.5
    ``cellular`` only: probability (0-1] that non-local material deposits at
    each hop.
cellular_nonlocal_max_hops : int, default=4
    ``cellular`` only: largest number of cells non-local material travels.
erodibility_field : Raster or numpy.ndarray or None, default=None
    Per-pixel absolute erodibility K replacing ``erodibility`` in the fluvial
    step: a Raster strictly on the DEM grid or a ``(n_rows, n_cols)`` array
    (NaN only on DEM nodata). Every valid pixel needs a finite K > 0.
erodibility_m_exponent : float or None, default=None
    The m the field was calibrated for; a different m raises ``ValueError``.
erodibility_area_convention : {"map_area", "specific_area"} or None, default=None
    Area convention of the field; ``map_area`` K is converted by dx**m.

Attributes
----------
coupling_regime : str
    Resolved coupling experiment: coupled or channels_as_boundaries.
elevation : Raster
    Current elevation Raster (m).
erodibility_field : object
    The per-pixel erodibility in use (run convention), or None.
hillslope_model : str
    Name of the hillslope model in use.
iteration : int
    Number of steps taken so far.
time_years : float
    Model time (years).

Methods
-------
channel_mask() -> Raster
    Return the imposed or currently threshold-derived channel mask.
run(n_steps: int, compute_erosion_rate: bool = False) -> LandscapeStepResult
    Advance the coupled model repeatedly and return the final step result.
set_erodibility_field(field: object | None) -> None
    Replace the per-pixel erodibility used by subsequent steps.
set_forcing(uplift_rate: float, baselevel_fall_rate: float = 0.0) -> None
    Change the uniform tectonic/base-level forcing used by subsequent steps.
step(compute_erosion_rate: bool = False) -> LandscapeStepResult
    Advance the coupled model by one configured timestep.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

Create a coupled landscape-evolution model from an in-memory DEM.

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Initial, depression-conditioned elevation surface.
timestep_years : float, optional
    Duration of each call to ``step``.
erodibility, m_exponent, n_exponent : float, optional
    Stream-power incision parameters. ``erodibility`` must be > 0; it is also the
    reference K for ``erodibility_field``.
uplift_rate, hillslope_diffusivity : float, optional
    Uniform uplift in m yr⁻¹ and hillslope diffusivity in m² yr⁻¹.
hillslope_model : {"none", "linear", "roering", "roering_implicit", "cidre", "adi", "cellular"}, optional
    Hillslope process model. ``none`` disables hillslope transport.
nonlinear_hillslopes, critical_hillslope_slope : bool, float, optional
    Roering nonlinear-flux controls.
incision_threshold_specific_area : float, optional
    Channel threshold in specific catchment area A/dx (metres); zero supports fully coupled runs.
coupling_regime : {"automatic", "coupled", "channels_as_boundaries"}, optional
    Whether hillslope channels emerge or are imposed.
boundary_conditions : str, optional
    Four NESW open, no-flux, periodic, or base-level codes.
fluvial_method : {"d8", "dinf", "none"}, optional
    Fluvial incision routing method, or ``none`` for hillslope-only evolution.
channel_mask : Raster, optional
    Same-grid binary imposed channel raster.
hold_channel_mask_fixed : bool, optional
    Add imposed channel pixels to the fixed-elevation set.
fixed_pixels : array-like of int, optional
    Explicit N-by-2 ``(row, col)`` fixed-elevation cells. Defaults to open/base-level edges.
n_threads : int, optional
    OpenMP thread count; zero uses the runtime default.
baselevel_fall_rate : float, optional
    Downward motion of fixed base-level cells in m yr⁻¹.
cellular_r_match, cellular_cfl_safety, cellular_nonlocal_fraction : float, optional
    Cellular-hillslope calibration, stability, and optional nonlocal-transfer controls.
erodibility_field : Raster or numpy.ndarray, optional
    Per-pixel absolute erodibility K replacing ``erodibility`` in the fluvial step: a
    Raster strictly on the DEM grid or a ``(n_rows, n_cols)`` array (NaN only on DEM
    nodata). Every valid pixel needs a finite K > 0.
erodibility_m_exponent : float, optional
    The m the field was calibrated for; a different m raises ``ValueError``.
erodibility_area_convention : {"map_area", "specific_area"}, optional
    Area convention of the field; ``map_area`` K is converted by dx**m.

Returns
-------
LandscapeModel
    Ready-to-step evolving model.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

exports.name: Raster
exports.doc:
An in-memory single-band float32 raster with an explicit validity mask.

Instances are value objects: functions in this module return new rasters and
do not modify their inputs. Values are float32; each pixel is either valid or
nodata (``mask_numpy()`` is True where valid). Array row 0 is the northern
edge (see ``RasterMeta``). Typical round trip::

    dem = lsdtt3.Raster.read("dem.tif")
    z = dem.to_numpy()                 # float32, shape (n_rows, n_cols)
    out = lsdtt3.Raster.from_numpy(z * 2, dem.mask_numpy(), dem.metadata)
    out.write("doubled.tif")

Not constructible directly; create one with ``Raster.from_numpy()`` or ``Raster.read()``. It is also returned by ``add()``, ``add_uniform_noise()``, ``aspect()``, ``breach_depressions()`` and 257 more.

Attributes
----------
metadata : RasterMeta
    Grid metadata (RasterMeta): shape, lower-left corner, cell size, nodata value, CRS.
shape : tuple[int, int]
    Grid shape as (n_rows, n_cols), the shape of to_numpy().
valid_pixel_count : int
    Number of valid (non-nodata) pixels.

Methods
-------
Raster.from_numpy(data: object, mask: object, metadata: RasterMeta) -> Raster
    Create a raster from copied two-dimensional NumPy-compatible arrays.
mask_numpy() -> object
    Return a copied Boolean array, True where raster values are valid.
Raster.read(path: str) -> Raster
    Read the first band of a GDAL-readable raster file.
to_numpy() -> object
    Return a copied ``float32`` array of raster values.
write(path: str, format: str = 'cog') -> None
    Write this raster to a file with GDAL.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

Create a raster from copied two-dimensional NumPy-compatible arrays.

Parameters

    Values with shape ``(metadata.n_rows, metadata.n_cols)``; row 0 is the
    northern edge. Copied and converted to float32.

    Same shape; True for valid pixels. False pixels are stored as
    ``metadata.nodata_value``. Use ``np.isfinite(data)`` or another raster's
    ``mask_numpy()``.

    raster's ``.metadata`` or ``RasterMeta.from_shape(...)``.

exports.name: RasterMeta
exports.doc:
Metadata describing a north-up, square-cell raster grid.

``x_min`` and ``y_min`` are the map coordinates of the lower-left (south-west)
corner of the grid, but array row 0 is the TOP (north) row, as in GDAL and
NumPy images: pixel ``(row, col)`` has its centre at
``x = x_min + (col + 0.5) * cell_size`` and
``y = y_max - (row + 0.5) * cell_size``. Coordinates and ``cell_size`` are in
the units of the CRS (metres for the projected CRSs lsdtt3 analyses need).
Every ``Raster`` and ``FlowInfo`` carries one as ``.metadata``; create one with
``RasterMeta.from_shape`` to build a raster from NumPy arrays.

Not constructible directly; create one with ``RasterMeta.from_shape()``. It is also returned by ``Raster.metadata``, ``FlowInfo.metadata``, ``FlowGraph.metadata``.

Attributes
----------
cell_size : float
    Square cell width and height, in CRS units (metres when projected).
crs_wkt : str
    Coordinate reference system as WKT; empty if none.
epsg_code : int
    EPSG code of the CRS if known, else 0.
is_valid : bool
    True if n_rows, n_cols and cell_size are all positive.
n_cols : int
    Number of columns (west to east).
n_pixels : int
    Total number of pixels, n_rows * n_cols (valid or not).
n_rows : int
    Number of rows (north to south).
nodata_value : float
    Value stored in invalid pixels.
pixel_area : float
    Area of one pixel, cell_size squared (m^2 for a metre CRS).
x_max : float
    Easting of the eastern edge: x_min + n_cols * cell_size.
x_min : float
    Easting of the western edge of the grid, in CRS units.
y_max : float
    Northing of the northern edge (the top of row 0): y_min + n_rows * cell_size.
y_min : float
    Northing of the southern edge of the grid (the bottom of the last row).

Methods
-------
RasterMeta.from_shape(n_rows: int, n_cols: int, x_min: float = 0.0, y_min: float = 0.0, cell_size: float = 1.0, nodata_value: float = -9999.0, crs_wkt: str = '', epsg_code: int = 0) -> RasterMeta
    Create raster metadata from a grid shape and the grid's lower-left corner.
lonlat_to_row_col(longitude: object, latitude: object, crs: str = 'EPSG:4326') -> tuple
    Return the ``(row, col)`` of the pixels containing longitude/latitude points.
row_col_to_xy(row: object, col: object) -> tuple
    Return the map coordinates ``(x, y)`` of pixel centres.
xy_to_row_col(x: object, y: object) -> tuple
    Return the ``(row, col)`` of the pixels containing map points ``(x, y)``.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

``x_min, y_min`` locate the lower-left (south-west) corner of the grid; the

members.doc:
lonlat_to_row_col(self, longitude: object, latitude: object, crs: str = 'EPSG:4326') -> tuple

Return the ``(row, col)`` of the pixels containing longitude/latitude points.

The points are transformed from ``crs`` into the grid's CRS (``crs_wkt``)
with GDAL/PROJ, then located as in ``xy_to_row_col``. Longitude comes first,
as x. To move a point onto a channel use ``FlowInfo.snap_points`` instead.

Parameters
----------
longitude, latitude : float or array-like of float
    Coordinates in decimal degrees (in ``crs`` units for a projected
    ``crs``). Arrays are broadcast against each other.
crs : str, default='EPSG:4326'
    CRS of the input points: an ``"EPSG:<code>"`` string, WKT or PROJ
    string; the default is WGS84 longitude/latitude.

Returns
-------
tuple of (int, int) or tuple of (numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray)
    ``(row, col)`` as in ``xy_to_row_col``; -1 for points off the grid or
    that cannot be projected. Raises ``ValueError`` if the grid has no CRS
    or ``crs`` is not understood.

Examples
--------
>>> dem = lsdtt3.fetch_dem(15.63, 37.88, 16.21, 38.31)
>>> row, col = dem.metadata.lonlat_to_row_col(15.79008, 37.94234)

members.name: row_col_to_xy
members.doc:
row_col_to_xy(self, row: object, col: object) -> tuple

Return the map coordinates ``(x, y)`` of pixel centres.

``x = x_min + (col + 0.5) * cell_size`` and
``y = y_max - (row + 0.5) * cell_size``: row 0 is the northern (top) edge, so
``y`` decreases as ``row`` increases.

Parameters
----------
row, col : int or array-like of int
    Zero-based pixel positions (rows north to south, columns west to east).
    Arrays are broadcast against each other. Positions are not checked
    against the grid: an off-grid position gives the centre the pixel would
    have.

Returns
-------
tuple of (float, float) or tuple of (numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray)
    ``(x, y)`` in the grid's CRS units (metres for a projected CRS): Python
    floats for scalar input, otherwise float64 arrays of the broadcast
    input shape.

Examples
--------
>>> meta = lsdtt3.RasterMeta.from_shape(100, 200, x_min=500000.0, y_min=4200000.0, cell_size=30.0)
>>> meta.row_col_to_xy(0, 1)
(500045.0, 4202985.0)

signatures.definition: def row_col_to_xy(self, row: object, col: object) -> tuple

members.doc: Easting of the western edge of the grid, in CRS units.

members.name: xy_to_row_col
members.doc:
xy_to_row_col(self, x: object, y: object) -> tuple

Return the ``(row, col)`` of the pixels containing map points ``(x, y)``.

A pixel covers ``x_min + col * cell_size <= x < x_min + (col + 1) * cell_size``
and ``y_max - (row + 1) * cell_size < y <= y_max - row * cell_size``, so row 0
is the northern (top) edge: ``col = floor((x - x_min) / cell_size)`` and
``row = floor((y_max - y) / cell_size)``. The inverse of ``row_col_to_xy`` for
pixel centres.

Parameters
----------
x, y : float or array-like of float
    Easting and northing in the grid's own CRS (``crs_wkt``; metres for a
    projected CRS). Arrays are broadcast against each other.

Returns
-------
tuple of (int, int) or tuple of (numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray)
    ``(row, col)``: Python ints for scalar input, otherwise int64 arrays of
    the broadcast input shape. Points outside the grid (including points on
    its eastern or southern boundary line) and non-finite coordinates give
    row = col = -1; they do not raise.

Examples
--------
>>> meta = lsdtt3.RasterMeta.from_shape(100, 200, x_min=500000.0, y_min=4200000.0, cell_size=30.0)
>>> meta.xy_to_row_col(500045.0, 4202985.0)
(0, 1)

exports.name: RotationFrame
exports.doc:
An oblique analysis frame aligned with a feature, and its rotate-back target.

A frame is a Hotine Oblique Mercator (variant B) CRS whose central line runs
along a fault, river, coastline or elongated range, with the feature along
+x and the frame centre at (0, 0). A raster in the frame is an ordinary
north-up raster in that CRS, so every lsdtt3 analysis runs on it unchanged,
on a grid that holds the strip rather than its bounding box. Bearings from
analyses are then clockwise from grid up (90 = along the feature) unless
``bearings_relative_to_true_north=True`` is passed.

The frame also carries the lattice that ``rotate_back`` writes products onto:
the source DEM's own grid for a frame built with ``source=``, else the UTM
(or polar stereographic) CRS of the frame centre on the lattice a fetch uses.
Bring back products (basins, channels, IDs), never the DEM.

Get one with ``RotationFrame.from_feature`` (a line, two points or polygon
file), ``RotationFrame.from_valid_data`` (the footprint of a raster's valid
cells), ``RotationFrame.read`` (a ``*_rotation_frame.txt`` written by a CLI
or by ``write``), or ``RotationFrame.from_raster`` (rebuilt from a frame
raster's own CRS when the frame file is lost). Typical use::

    frame = lsdtt3.RotationFrame.from_feature("fault.gpkg", width=10000.0,
                                              grid_spacing=30.0)
    dem = lsdtt3.fetch_dem(frame=frame, grid_spacing=30.0)
    frame.write("fault_rotation_frame.txt")
    # ... analysis on dem ...
    basins_utm = lsdtt3.rotate_back(basins, frame, resampling="near")

Property names spell out the units of the frame-file keys: ``centre_lon`` is
``centre_longitude``, ``azimuth_deg`` is ``azimuth_degrees``, ``width_m`` is
``width_metres``, ``target_crs_epsg`` is ``target_epsg``, and so on.

Not constructible directly; create one with ``RotationFrame.from_feature()`` or ``RotationFrame.from_raster()`` or ``RotationFrame.from_valid_data()`` or ``RotationFrame.read()``.

Attributes
----------
axis_length_metres : float
    Geodesic length of the axis between its end points (without the end buffer), m.
azimuth_degrees : float
    Azimuth of the axis at the centre, clockwise from true north, in (-90, 90].
base_crs_wkt : str
    WKT of the geographic CRS (datum) the frame is built on.
buffer_all_sides : bool
    True when the end buffer is also on both long sides (polygon frames).
cell_size : float
    Frame cell size, m.
centre_latitude : float
    Latitude of the frame centre, degrees in the base geographic CRS.
centre_longitude : float
    Longitude of the frame centre, degrees in the base geographic CRS.
crs_wkt : str
    The frame CRS as WKT.
end_buffer_metres : float
    Length added beyond each axis end (and each long side for a polygon), m.
end_points : tuple
    The axis end points ((lon, lat), (lon, lat)), west one first.
extent : tuple
    Frame extent (x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max) in frame metres.
feature_fname : str
    File name of the feature the frame was built from, or empty.
feature_layer : str
    Layer of the feature file the frame was built from, or empty.

    How the frame was defined: line, two_points, polygon, data_footprint or crs.

members.name: from_feature
members.doc:
from_feature(path: str, width: float = 0.0, end_buffer: float = -1.0, grid_spacing: float = 0.0, layer: str = '', source: object | None = None, target_epsg: int = 0) -> lsdtt3.RotationFrame

Build the frame of a line, two-point or polygon feature file.

A line (or a multi-part line) uses its two furthest end points as the axis;
two points are the axis ends; a polygon uses its minimum-area enclosing
rectangle, longest side as the axis, and takes its width from the polygon.
The same routine as ``fetch_from_linear_feature`` in lsdtt-fetch-raster
and ``rotate_to_linear_feature`` in lsdtt-raster-preprocessing.

Parameters
----------
path : str
    Feature file (any OGR vector: GeoPackage, GeoJSON, shapefile, ...), in
    any CRS.
width : float, default=0.0
    Full width of the strip across the axis, in metres. Required (> 0) for
    a line or two points; ignored, with a warning, for a polygon.
end_buffer : float, default=-1.0
    Length added beyond each axis end, in metres (on all four sides for a
    polygon). Negative means 10 cells.
grid_spacing : float, default=0.0
    Frame cell size in metres. Without ``source``, 0 means 30 m (the
    ``fetch_dem`` default). With ``source``, 0 means the source's own cell
    size when it is projected in metres, else the size reprojection would
    choose, as lsdtt-raster-preprocessing does.
layer : str, default=""
    Layer to read; empty reads the first layer (warned if there are several).
source : Raster or None, default=None
    The DEM this frame will rotate (``rotate_to_frame``). The frame is built
    on its geographic datum, and the rotate-back target is its own grid
    (CRS, cell size and lower-left corner) when it is projected in metres.
    None builds a frame for ``fetch_dem`` on WGS84.
target_epsg : int, default=0
    Without ``source`` only: EPSG code of the rotate-back target. 0 picks the
    UTM (or polar stereographic beyond 75 degrees) CRS of the frame centre.

Returns
-------
RotationFrame
    The frame. Reader and builder notes (several layers, an ill-defined
    polygon axis) are issued as ``UserWarning``; a file that cannot be read
    or used raises ``ValueError``.

Rebuild the frame of a raster that is already in an lsdtt3 oblique frame.

The fallback when the frame file is lost: the frame comes from the raster's
own CRS and extent, and the rotate-back target is the UTM (or polar

``UserWarning`` says that a source DEM origin off that lattice cannot be
recovered without the frame file.

RotationFrame

from_valid_data(source: lsdtt3.Raster, end_buffer: float = -1.0, grid_spacing: float = 0.0) -> lsdtt3.RotationFrame

Build the frame of a raster's valid cells (its minimum-area rectangle).

The polygon of the outer corners of the first and last valid cell of every
row, framed as a polygon feature would be; the frame of
``rotate_to_data_footprint`` in lsdtt-raster-preprocessing. A footprint with
no clear long axis (a square DEM) is warned.

Parameters
----------
source : Raster
    The DEM; it must have a CRS. The rotate-back target is its own grid
    when it is projected in metres.
end_buffer : float, default=-1.0
    Length added on all four sides, in metres; negative means 10 cells.
grid_spacing : float, default=0.0
    Frame cell size in metres; 0 chooses it from ``source`` as
    ``from_feature`` does.

Returns
-------
RotationFrame
    The frame; ``ValueError`` for a raster with no CRS or no valid cells.

relative_elevation(self, dem: lsdtt3.Raster, relative_elevation_domain_algorithm_choice: str = 'valley_mask', domain_mask: object | None = None, relative_elevation_max_distance_metres: float = 0.0) -> tuple

Relative elevation above the valley centrelines' baselines (REM).

lsdtt-valley-centreline ``write_relative_elevation_raster``. On the valley
floor each cell is measured against the centreline node of the largest
channel whose floor it lies on; elsewhere against the node reached by the
shortest floor-width-scaled ground distance. Needs centrelines from a
``ChannelScope`` or :func:`build_valley_width_network` (the channels are
ranked by drainage area).

----------

    Elevation (m), the DEM the centrelines were made on.
relative_elevation_domain_algorithm_choice : {"valley_mask", "supplied", "whole_dem"}, default="valley_mask"
    Where the field is computed: the valley floor, ``domain_mask``, or
    every valid cell. The floor is always included.
domain_mask : Raster or None, default=None
    Cells > 0.5, for ``supplied``.
relative_elevation_max_distance_metres : float, default=0.0
    Largest ground distance (m) from a cell to its node; 0 means none.

Returns

tuple of Raster
    ``(relative_elevation, owner)``: elevation above the owning node's
    baseline (m) and the owning centreline's ``source_id``; nodata outside
    the domain and the floor.

exports.doc:
Compute polyfit aspect in degrees; lambda_metres defaults to three cells.

Aspect is the downslope direction the surface faces, in compass degrees

exports.name: breach_least_cost
exports.doc:
Breach depressions along least-cost paths (Lindsay 2020).

A port of WhiteboxTools BreachDepressionsLeastCost (whitebox_workflows 2.0.6).

Parameters
----------
raster : Raster
    Elevation raster (m).
max_distance : int or None, default=None
    Maximum breach path length in cells, counted in steps from the pit (a
    diagonal step counts as one). 1 to 32767. None selects the edge policy's
    default: 1000 for ``outlet`` (long enough to bridge large water bodies)
    and 100 for ``whitebox`` (the WhiteboxTools default).
max_cost : float, optional
    A pit whose cheapest path costs more is left unbreached. The cost is the
    depth each path cell is lowered, summed: metres, or metres x cells when
    ``prefer_shortest_path`` is true. Default unlimited.
prefer_shortest_path : bool, default=False
    Weight each step's cost by its length in cells, favouring shorter paths.
flat_increment : float, default=0
    Elevation drop (m) per cell along a breach channel. 0 or less selects twice
    the float32 spacing at the largest absolute elevation.
fill_remainder : bool, default=True
    Fill what the breach leaves (Priority-Flood with ``fill_min_slope``) so
    every interior cell has a lower neighbour.
n_threads : int, default=0
    Ignored; the algorithm is serial.
edge_policy : {"outlet", "whitebox"}, default="outlet"
    ``outlet``: the raster edge is an outlet, like a nodata cell.
    ``whitebox``: as in WhiteboxTools, a breach must reach an edge cell that
    is already low enough.
fill_min_slope : float, default=0.0001
    Gradient (m/m) imposed by the remainder fill.

Returns
-------
Raster
    New in-memory raster; save it with ``.write(path)``.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

Classify flat surfaces using a ``ChannelScope``: the HAND ladder of
``lsdtt-fluvial-surfaces``.

HAND, its nearest-channel donors, flow distance, channel mask, and source IDs
are derived from the scope's retained D8 flow topology. Pixels are banded by
HAND in reach windows along each channel (the reference-field ladder), each
band is labelled into patches, and patches are classed floodplain or
terrace. The ladder keywords have the names and meanings of the
lsdtt-fluvial-surfaces parameters; see that CLI's reference for the method.
Three defaults differ from the CLI so earlier results are unchanged:
``min_band_component_pixels`` (CLI 50),
``ladder_unresolved_window_algorithm_choice`` (CLI ``nearest_resolved``) and
``valley_corridor_half_width_metres`` (CLI 5000).

Parameters

    Gradient (m/m) between gentle and steep.

    fraction of the smaller flanking peak.

    Gap finder: a local minimum is a candidate break when its floor is below

    Reject a partition whose worst break sits where the density is above

exports.name: classify_floodplain_terraces_by_thresholds
exports.doc:
Floodplains and terraces from a HAND bound and a gradient bound (Clubb et al. 2017).

The classifier of lsdtt-fluvial-surfaces' ``clubb2017`` method and of
lsdtt-hillslope-channel-coupling's floodplain rule. Floodplain: admitted
cells with HAND below ``max_floodplain_hand_metres`` and gradient below
``max_floodplain_gradient`` (when > 0), plus the channel cells when
``seed_channel_pixels``; 8-connected components smaller than
``min_band_component_pixels`` are dropped, and with
``require_channel_contact`` only components containing a channel cell are
kept. Terraces (``find_terraces``): admitted, non-floodplain cells of
gentle gradient whose ``terrace_field`` lies more than
``min_terrace_height_above_floodplain_metres`` above the floodplain bound
and at most ``max_terrace_height_metres`` (when > 0). Pick the bounds from
the data with :func:`select_threshold`.

Parameters
----------
admitted : Raster
    Cells > 0.5 may be floodplain or terrace; its mask is the output domain.
hand : Raster
    Height above the channel (m), co-registered.
channel_mask : Raster
    Channel cells (> 0.5), for seeding and the contact test.
gradient : Raster or None, default=None
    Gradient (m/m); required when ``max_floodplain_gradient`` > 0.
terrace_field : Raster or None, default=None
    The terrace reference (HAND, or :func:`relief_above_nearest_baseline`);
    required with ``find_terraces``.
max_floodplain_hand_metres : float, default=0.0
    Floodplain HAND bound (m).
max_floodplain_gradient : float, default=0.0
    Floodplain gradient bound (m/m); 0 applies none.
seed_channel_pixels, require_channel_contact : bool, default=True
    Add the channel cells to the floodplain; keep only components that
    contain one.
min_band_component_pixels : int, default=0
    Smallest component kept (pixels); 0 or 1 keeps all.
fill_floodplain_holes : bool, default=False
    Fill holes in the floodplain components.
find_terraces : bool, default=False
    Also classify terraces.
min_terrace_height_above_floodplain_metres : float, default=0.0
    Terraces start this far (m, >= 0) above the floodplain bound.
max_terrace_height_metres : float, default=0.0
    Terrace ceiling (m) of ``terrace_field``; 0 means none.

Returns
-------
FloodplainThresholdResult

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

exports.name: classify_surface_shape
exports.doc:
Compute polyfit principal curvatures, then classify surface shape.

This function has 2 call forms:

1. ``classify_surface_shape(raster: Raster, lambda_metres: float = 0.0, z_factor: float = 1.0, n_threads: int = 0, kt: float = 0.0) -> dict``

   Compute polyfit principal curvatures, then classify surface shape.

2. ``classify_surface_shape(maximum_curvature: Raster, minimum_curvature: Raster, kt: float = 0.0) -> dict``

   Classify surface shape from existing principal-curvature rasters.

Parameters
----------
raster : Raster
    Elevation raster (m) in a projected metre CRS.
lambda_metres : float, default=0.0
    Polyfit length scale (m), as in ``polyfit_metrics``; 0 uses three cells.
z_factor : float, default=1.0
    Elevation scale factor.
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.
kt : float, default=0.0
    Call form 1: Curvature threshold (1/m): principal curvatures with magnitude <= kt
    count as zero (flat in that direction).
    Call form 2: Curvature threshold (1/m) below which a curvature counts as zero.
maximum_curvature, minimum_curvature : Raster
    Principal curvatures k_max and k_min (1/m), for example from
    ``polyfit_metrics`` or ``fundamental_form_principal_curvatures``.

Returns
-------
dict[str, Raster]
    Call form 1: ``"shape_class"``: SMAP class codes -4 perfect saddle, -3 basin
    (bowl), -2 synformal saddle, -1 synform (valley), 0 plane, 1 antiform
    (ridge), 2 antiformal saddle, 3 peak (dome); ``"gaussian_curvature"``
    (1/m^2) and ``"mean_curvature"`` (1/m) after the kt threshold.
dict[str, Raster]
    Call form 2: ``"shape_class"`` (codes as in the first call form),
    ``"gaussian_curvature"`` (1/m^2) and ``"mean_curvature"`` (1/m).

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

exports.name: cluster_surface_levels
exports.doc:
Group surface heights into levels and test whether they cluster.

The test behind lsdtt-fluvial-surfaces' ``write_patch_level_clusters_csv``:
sorted heights are split wherever consecutive values are at least
``required_gap_metres`` apart. The statistic is the empty fraction, the
share of the height range taken by those gaps, compared with ``n_null``
samples of as many heights drawn uniformly over the same range:
``p = (1 + #{null >= observed}) / (1 + n_null)``. A small p says the
heights sit on levels more than random heights would.

Parameters
----------
values : Raster or array-like of float
    Heights (m), for example the ``median_field`` of
    ``FlatSurfaceClassification.patches``.
required_gap_metres : float
    Gap (m, > 0) that separates two levels, typically kappa x E_v.
n_null : int, default=999
    Number of uniform null samples.
seed : int, default=1
    Random seed of the null samples.

Returns
-------
dict
    ``clusters`` (DataFrame: lower_metres, upper_metres, centre_metres (the
    median), n_values, ascending), ``n_values``, ``empty_fraction``,
    ``null_mean_empty_fraction``, ``p_value`` (1 with fewer than 3 values)
    and ``n_null``.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

signatures.definition: def cluster_surface_levels(values: object, required_gap_metres: float, n_null: int = \0, seed: int = \1) -> dict

exports.name: coherence_diffusion
exports.doc:
Coherence-enhancing diffusion: smoothing along linear features.

Smooths along the local feature orientation from the structure tensor and
little across it, bridging and denoising ridges, valleys and scarps.
time_step must be in (0, 0.25]. A radius of 0 means one cell
(derivative_radius_metres) or three cells (integration_radius_metres).
contrast sets how selective the along-feature smoothing is; min_diffusivity
is the across-feature floor, in (0, 1). The same smoothing as
smooth_algorithm_choice: coherence_diffusion in lsdtt-raster-preprocessing.

Parameters
----------
raster : Raster
    Elevation raster (m).
n_iterations : int, default=10
    Number of diffusion iterations.
time_step : float, default=0.15
    Explicit time step, in (0, 0.25].
derivative_radius_metres : float, default=0.0
    Smoothing radius (m) of the gradients; 0 means one cell.
integration_radius_metres : float, default=0.0
    Radius (m) over which the structure tensor is averaged; 0 means three
    cells.
contrast : float, default=0.2
    How selective the along-feature smoothing is.
min_diffusivity : float, default=0.001
    Across-feature diffusivity floor, in (0, 1).
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.

Returns
-------
Raster
    Smoothed DEM (m).

Authors
-------
S. M. Mudd
B. Gailleton

exports.name: compare_bearings
exports.doc:
Compare two samples of bearings or axial orientations.

NaN and infinite values are ignored. The result combines the existing native
Kuiper two-sample test with circular Wasserstein distance.

    Bearing samples in degrees.
axial : bool, default=False
    Treat angles 180 degrees apart as equivalent orientations.
rotation_invariant : bool, default=False
    Allow a single global rotation of ``second`` when computing the
    Wasserstein distance. The Kuiper statistic always retains absolute phase.

Returns

dict
    Sample sizes, period, circular Wasserstein distance, optional optimal
    rotation, and Kuiper statistic with its approximate p-value.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
