exports.name: coregister_dem
exports.doc:
Coregister a DEM to a reference with the Nuth and Kaab (2011) method.

Iteratively fits the horizontal and vertical shift that best explains the
elevation differences as a function of aspect, and applies it to moving.
Both rasters must be on the same grid (use reproject_to_grid first). The same
coregistration as run_dem_coregistration in lsdtt-raster-calculator, with
its defaults.

Parameters
----------
reference : Raster
    Reference DEM (m).
moving : Raster
    DEM (m) to shift, on the same grid as ``reference``.
max_iterations : int, default=8
    Largest number of Nuth-Kaab iterations.
offset_threshold_pixels : float, default=0.001
    Stop when an iteration's horizontal step is below this (pixels).
aspect_bin_count : int, default=72
    Number of aspect bins in the fit.
min_samples : int, default=500
    Smallest number of valid samples required.
subsample_count : int, default=500000
    Largest number of pixels sampled per iteration.
apply_vertical_shift : bool, default=True
    Also remove the vertical offset dz.
max_horizontal_step_metres : float, default=0.0
    Cap (m) on each iteration's horizontal step; 0 means none.
initial_dx_metres, initial_dy_metres, initial_dz_metres : float, default=0.0
    Starting shift (m) in x, y and z.

Returns
-------
dict
    ``"raster"`` (moving, shifted), ``"dx_metres"``, ``"dy_metres"``,
    ``"dz_metres"`` (the total shift, m), ``"iterations"``, ``"converged"``
    and ``"diagnostics"`` (a pandas DataFrame with one row per iteration).

Authors
-------
S. M. Mudd
B. Gailleton

exports.name: crn_invert_basin_erosion
exports.doc:
Invert basin-mean erosion rates from a point GeoDataFrame.

Points are projected to the flow-grid CRS, snapped to the nearest D8 channel
meeting ``channel_threshold_pixels``, then inverted with the native CAIRN
solver over each snapped outlet's exact upslope pixel set. Failed rows remain
in the returned GeoDataFrame and are identified by ``crn_status``.

----------

    the flow grid's CRS) with a concentration column.
production_scaling : Raster
    Production-scaling factor on the flow grid (``crn_production_scaling``).
concentration_column : str, default="concentration"
    Column of measured concentrations in atoms/g (positive).
nuclide : {"Be10", "Al26", "C14"}, default="Be10"
    Cosmogenic nuclide.
muon_scheme : str, default="BraucherBorchers"
    Muon production parameterisation: ``"Braucher"``,
    ``"BraucherBorchers"``, ``"Granger"``, ``"Schaller"`` or
    ``"newCRONUS"``.
channel_threshold_pixels : int, default=1000

    pixels (positive).
snap_radius_pixels : int, default=25

topographic_shielding : Raster or None, default=None
    Topographic shielding factor (dimensionless, 0-1; 1 = unshielded) on the
    same grid; None means 1 everywhere.
snow_shielding : Raster or None, default=None
    Snow shielding as an effective depth (g/cm^2); None means 0 (no snow).
self_shielding : Raster or None, default=None

exports.name: detect_directional_periodicity
exports.doc:
Detect local regularly spaced parallel features with sliding-window FFTs.

Families of evenly spaced parallel lines (ditches, tracks, cultivation
ridges) give a sharp peak in the 2D power spectrum at 1 / spacing. A
window slides over the raster and the strongest peak in the spacing band
is recorded; each pixel keeps its best window.

Parameters
----------
raster : Raster
    Input raster, for example a DEM or a curvature response.
window_size_pixels : int
    Window side (pixels, >= 8); should span several of the largest spacings.
step_pixels : int
    Window stride (pixels, >= 1), typically half the window.
min_spacing_metres, max_spacing_metres : float
    Range of spacings (m) searched; the minimum must exceed 2 cell sizes and
    the maximum be below the window extent.
min_valid_fraction : float, default=0.6
    Windows with a smaller fraction of valid pixels are skipped.
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.
bearings_relative_to_true_north : bool, default=False
    Convert ``orientation_degrees`` to true north at each pixel, as the
    CLI's ``bearings_relative_to_true_north``; needs a raster with a CRS.

Returns
-------
dict
    ``"strength"`` (peak prominence), ``"spacing_metres"`` and
    ``"orientation_degrees"`` (line orientation, 0-180, clockwise from grid
    north or true north) Rasters.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

exports.name: divide_migration
exports.doc:
Compare channel-head elevation, chi, relief, and gradient across adjacent outlet-defined basin divides.

Basins are defined by the supplied outlets (grouped into units by
``clusters``); for every pair of adjacent units the channel heads on either
side of their shared divide are compared, as evidence for the direction of
divide migration.

Parameters
----------
flow : FlowInfo
    Flow topology of the conditioned DEM.
dem : Raster
    The conditioned DEM (m) on the flow grid.
outlets : array-like of int
    N x 2 array of ``(row, col)`` outlet pixels (at least two).
clusters : array-like or None, default=None
    One label per outlet grouping outlets into units (outlets with the same
    label form one side); None makes every outlet its own unit.
source_pixels : int, default=1000
    Channel threshold (contributing pixels) for sources, snapping and chi.
snapping : {"downstream", "none"}, default="downstream"
    Snap outlets downstream onto the channel network, or use them as given.
outlet_control : {"none", "complete_only", "elevation", "max_out_elevation"}, default="complete_only"
    ``complete_only``: drop basins touching nodata or an open edge;
    ``elevation``: drop outlets below ``min_outlet_elevation``;
    ``max_out_elevation``: put every basin on a common base level (the
    highest outlet elevation) before comparing chi; ``none``: no control.
min_outlet_elevation : float, default=-inf
    Lowest outlet elevation (m) kept by ``outlet_control="elevation"``.
m_over_n : float, default=0.45
    Concavity index for chi (positive).
reference_area : float, default=1.0
    Chi reference area A0 (m^2, positive).
uncertainty : {"std_err", "std_dev", "bootstrap", "ttest"}, default="std_err"
    How the uncertainty of each across-divide difference is reported.

    Replicates for ``uncertainty="bootstrap"``.

    Random seed for the bootstrap.

    channel-head and pair-summary tables.

exports.name: extract_channel_heads
exports.doc:
Extract D8 channel heads by drainage threshold or Wiener curvature.

``method='threshold'`` returns the upstream ends of all pixels with at least
``threshold_contributing_pixels`` contributing pixels (as
``FlowInfo.sources``). ``method='wiener'`` Wiener-filters the DEM, computes
tangential curvature, keeps pixels whose positive curvature exceeds a
quantile-quantile threshold, prunes by drainage area and component size,
thins the mask to a skeleton and uses its end points as heads; it requires
FFTW and a projected-metre DEM. With ``diagnostics=True``, the result
retains the filtered DEM, tangential curvature, candidate channel mask,
skeleton, and QQ table.

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Elevation (m) on the flow grid (same grid and validity mask).
flow : FlowInfo
    Flow topology built from the (conditioned) DEM.
method : {"threshold", "wiener"}, default="threshold"
    Head-detection method.
threshold_contributing_pixels : int, default=1000
    ``"threshold"`` only: channel threshold in contributing pixels
    (including self); positive.
pruning_drainage_area_m2 : float, default=1000.0
    ``"wiener"`` only: candidate channel pixels with a smaller D8 drainage
    area (m^2) are removed.
surface_fitting_radius_metres : float, default=6.0
    ``"wiener"`` only: polyfit length scale (m) used for curvature, as
    ``lambda_metres`` in ``polyfit_metrics``.
connected_components_threshold_pixels : int, default=100
    ``"wiener"`` only: connected channel patches with fewer pixels (D8
    connectivity) are removed.
diagnostics : bool, default=False
    ``"wiener"`` only: keep the intermediate rasters and QQ table.

Returns
-------
ChannelHeads
    Head pixels and (optionally) diagnostics.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

exports.doc:
Extract long smooth road-like ribbons from a DEM.

Road surfaces are smoother than the surrounding terrain: smoothness is
computed from local roughness, a path opening keeps only long smooth
ribbons, and small components are removed.

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Elevation raster (m), usually a high-resolution lidar DEM.
roughness_radius_metres : float, default=1.5
    Radius (m) of the local elevation-range window.

exports.name: extract_valley_centrelines
exports.doc:
Route centrelines through a supplied valley mask using a resolved ``ChannelScope``.

This function has 2 call forms:

1. ``extract_valley_centrelines(dem: Raster, scope: ChannelScope, corridor_width_metres: float = 5000.0, fallback_valley_hand_metres: object | None = None, valley_dilation_pixels: int = 4, trough_scaling_factor: float = 0.1, centreline_loops: int = 5, n_threads: int = 0, *, valley_mask: Raster, centreline_baseline_algorithm_choice: str = 'projected_monotonic') -> ValleyCentrelineResult``

   Route centrelines through a supplied valley mask using a resolved ``ChannelScope``.

2. ``extract_valley_centrelines(dem: Raster, channels: object, corridor_width_metres: float = 5000.0, fallback_valley_hand_metres: object | None = None, valley_dilation_pixels: int = 4, trough_scaling_factor: float = 0.1, centreline_loops: int = 5, n_threads: int = 0, *, valley_mask: Raster, centreline_baseline_algorithm_choice: str = 'projected_monotonic') -> ValleyCentrelineResult``

   Route centrelines through a supplied valley mask from ordered channel paths.

   ``channels`` is a sequence of upstream-to-downstream ``(row, col)`` arrays.
   A synthetic trough is carved into the valley floor, deepest along the
   valley axis, and flow is routed down it, so the centreline follows the
   middle of the valley rather than the channel. This function has two call
   forms: pass a ``ChannelScope`` as ``scope`` (its traced channels are used) or
   the ordered channel paths as ``channels``.

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Elevation raster (m).
scope : ChannelScope
    First call form: channels resolved by ``FlowInfo.channel_scope``.
channels : sequence of numpy.ndarray
    Second call form: N x 2 ``(row, col)`` arrays, upstream to downstream.
corridor_width_metres : float, default=5000.0
    Half-width (m) of the corridor around each channel searched for valley
    pixels.
fallback_valley_hand_metres : float or None, default=None
    Deprecated and ignored when ``valley_mask`` is supplied (a
    ``DeprecationWarning`` is emitted if set).
valley_dilation_pixels : int, default=4
    Pixels by which valley patches are dilated (towards the channel only) to
    fill holes.
trough_scaling_factor : float, default=0.1
    Gradient (m/m) of the synthetic trough carved towards the valley axis:
    the trough is lowered by this times the distance to the valley wall
    (Clubb et al. 2022 method); doubled on retries.
centreline_loops : int, default=5
    Number of trough-carving and routing iterations.
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.
valley_mask : Raster, keyword-only
    0/1 valley-floor raster on the DEM grid, for example from
    ``find_valleys`` or ``valley_mask_from_cross_sections``.
centreline_baseline_algorithm_choice : {"projected_monotonic", "channel_crossings"}, default="projected_monotonic"
    How each centreline's baseline elevation is pinned to its channel, as
    in lsdtt-valley-centreline: channel elevations projected onto the
    centreline and made non-increasing, or pinned only where the centreline
    crosses the channel.

Returns
-------
ValleyCentrelineResult

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

exports.name: extract_valley_cross_sections
exports.doc:
Extract straight or boundary-fitted valley cross sections.

Optional curvature, hillshade, and channel-mask rasters enable feature picks.
Hydraulic break picks are always available; set ``compute_hydraulic_depth`` to
retain the full per-stage hydraulic-geometry curve.

Stations are placed along each centreline and a transect is cast across the
valley at each; all transects of a channel have the same length (a multiple
of its widest valley width).

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Elevation raster (m).
centrelines : ValleyCentrelineResult
    From :func:`extract_valley_centrelines`.
spacing_metres : float, default=500.0
    Spacing (m) of stations along the centreline (positive).
half_length_multiplier : float, default=1.5
    Transect total length as a multiple of the channel's widest bounded
    valley width (positive).
min_half_length_metres : float, default=0.0
    Floor (m) on the transect half-length; 0 means none.
max_half_length_metres : float, default=5000.0
    Cap (m) on the outward search for a valley side and on the half-length.
tangent_window_nodes : int, default=8
    Centreline nodes on each side used to smooth the local direction.
sample_step_metres : float, default=0.0
    Sample spacing (m) along a transect; 0 uses the cell size.
curved_sections : bool, default=False
    Trace boundary-fitted sections that curve through bends instead of
    straight transects.
curvature, hillshade : Raster or None, default=None
    Optional rasters sampled along transects for feature picks.
channel_mask : Raster or None, default=None
    Optional 0/1 channel raster for channel-crossing picks.
side_gap_tolerance_steps : int, default=1
    Out-of-valley steps tolerated before a valley side is declared.
feature_peak_min_prominence_fraction : float, default=0.15
    Minimum peak prominence, as a fraction of the profile range.
feature_peak_edge_margin_samples : int, default=2
    Ignore peaks this close (samples) to the transect ends.
clip_overlapping_sections : bool, default=True
    Clip transects where they would cross neighbouring sections.
neighbour_clip_window : int, default=2
    Number of neighbouring stations on each side considered for clipping.
min_section_reach_fraction : float, default=0.35
    Drop a station whose clipped length is below this fraction of the full
    transect length.
curved_wall_clearance_fraction : float, default=0.10
    Curved sections only: a clipped side still extends at least this
    fraction beyond the valley wall.
curved_streamwise_smoothing_passes : int, default=40
    Curved sections only: smoothing passes of the along-valley coordinate.
curved_coarse_spacing_metres : float, default=700.0
    Curved sections only: spacing (m) of the first, coarse set of stations
    before midpoints are added.
hydraulic_stage_step_metres : float, default=0.1
    Flood-stage increment (m) used to build width against stage.
hydraulic_min_step_height_metres : float, default=2.0
    Minimum height (m) between accepted hydraulic step boundaries.
hydraulic_min_step_width_pixels : int, default=3
    Minimum width change (pixels) between accepted step boundaries.
hydraulic_midpoint_search_samples : int, default=81
    Search resolution for placing each step midpoint.
hydraulic_min_crossings_preferred : int, default=2
    Preferred number of profile crossings at a step midpoint (2 = one bank
    pair).
compute_hydraulic_depth : bool, default=False
    Store the full stage / width / area / hydraulic-depth curve of each
    section (``hydraulic_curve``; Delchiaro et al. 2025 BankfullMapper).

Returns
-------
ValleyCrossSections

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

exports.name: fetch_dem
exports.doc:
Fetch a DEM for a WGS84 bounding box as an in-memory projected raster.

The source tiles are downloaded, mosaicked and warped to a projected grid
(UTM by default), with the same code and the same parameter names as
``lsdtt-fetch-raster``. The Copernicus DEM (the default ``cop30_aws``
source) stores the sea as exactly 0 m, not as nodata, so mask it before
flow routing: ``dem = mask_to_nodata(dem, 0.0)``. Cells outside the source
footprint are nodata.

Besides the global 30 m sources there are keyless national and polar
high-resolution DEMs (``us_3dep``, ``arctic_arcticdem``,
``antarctic_rema``, ``no_dtm``, ``nl_ahn``, ``es_mdt``, ``pl_nmt``,
``ca_hrdem``, ``ch_swissalti3d``, ``nz_lidar``, ``gb_sct_lidar``,
``jp_gsi``); ``dem_sources()`` lists each one's resolutions, surface models
(DSM or DTM), vertical datum, coverage and attribution. Warnings from the
fetch (partial coverage, overviews read, a LERC-compressed source this GDAL
cannot read, older Scottish collections covering the area) are issued as
``UserWarning``.

Or, with ``frame`` (a ``RotationFrame``) or ``fetch_from_linear_feature``,
fetch a strip along a fault, river or range warped straight from the source
tiles into an oblique frame (one resampling pass), with the feature along
+x. The return type is always ``Raster``; keep the ``RotationFrame`` to
rotate products back with ``rotate_back``.

Parameters
----------
west, south, east, north : float, optional
    WGS84 bounds in decimal degrees (longitude west/east, latitude
    south/north). Antimeridian-crossing requests are not supported:
    ``west`` must be less than ``east``. ``VectorBounds.bbox`` from
    ``bounds_from_vector`` can be unpacked here: ``fetch_dem(*b.bbox)``.
    Required unless ``frame`` or ``fetch_from_linear_feature`` gives the
    area; refused with them.
source : str, optional
    ``cop30_aws`` (default) is a keyless global 30 m Copernicus DEM.
    OpenTopography reads its key only from the ``OT_API_KEY`` or
    ``OT_API_KEY_FILE`` environment variables (never pass a key as an
    argument). ``planetary_computer`` is keyless. The national and polar
    sources are listed by ``dem_sources()``.
target_epsg : int, optional
    Output EPSG code. Zero selects the UTM zone of the bounding-box centre.
grid_spacing : float or None, optional
    Output cell size in target CRS units (m for UTM). None (default) uses
    the frame's cell size with ``frame``, the source's native resolution
    (``source_resolution_metres`` if set) for a national or polar source,
    and 30 otherwise. Output cells are always square.
resampling : str, optional
    GDAL warp resampling method (``"cubic"`` default, ``"bilinear"``,
    ``"near"``, ...).
nodata_value : float, optional
    Nodata value of the output (default -9999).
size_pixels : int, optional
    If > 0, crop an exact ``size_pixels`` x ``size_pixels`` square from the
    centre of the warped grid; 0 keeps the full extent.
cache_dir : str, optional
    Persistent cache directory. This is the only optional disk output; the
    returned raster itself is kept in memory. Empty means no caching.
ot_dem_type : str, optional
    OpenTopography dataset, for example ``"COP30"``, ``"SRTMGL1"``,
    ``"NASADEM"`` (see ``opentopography_datasets()``); other sources ignore it.
pc_collection, pc_asset : str, optional
    Planetary Computer STAC collection and asset key (defaults
    ``"cop-dem-glo-30"`` and ``"data"``); other sources ignore them.
http_timeout_seconds : int, optional
    Total time limit per HTTP request in seconds.
http_connect_timeout_seconds : int, optional
    Connection time limit per HTTP request in seconds.
http_max_retry : int, optional
    Number of retries of a failed HTTP request.
frame : RotationFrame or None, optional
    Fetch the frame's rectangle, warped into the frame. ``grid_spacing``,
    if given, must equal ``frame.cell_size``; ``target_epsg`` and ``size_pixels``
    are refused (the frame carries its rotate-back target).
fetch_from_linear_feature : bool, optional
    Build the frame from ``fetch_feature_fname`` here, as lsdtt-fetch-raster
    does; the same as ``frame=RotationFrame.from_feature(fetch_feature_fname,
    linear_feature_fetch_width, linear_feature_fetch_end_buffer,
    grid_spacing, fetch_feature_layer)``, which is the frame to keep for
    ``rotate_back``.
fetch_feature_fname : str, optional
    Line, two-point or polygon file (any OGR format and CRS).
fetch_feature_layer : str, optional
    Layer of the feature file; empty reads the first.
linear_feature_fetch_width : float, optional
    Full strip width in metres; required for a line or two points.
linear_feature_fetch_end_buffer : float, optional
    Length beyond each axis end in metres (all sides for a polygon);
    negative means 10 cells.
rotate_after_fetch : bool, optional
    With ``fetch_from_linear_feature``: True (default) returns the strip in
    the oblique frame; False returns the frame's WGS84 envelope in UTM, as a
    plain fetch.
source_resolution_metres : float, optional
    Native resolution (m) to fetch from a source that offers several (for
    example 1, 2 or 10 for ``arctic_arcticdem``); 0 (default) uses the
    source's default. Refused for a source that does not offer it.
surface_model_choice : {"source_default", "dtm", "dsm"}, optional
    Terrain (DTM) or surface (DSM) model. ``source_default`` takes the DTM
    where the source has one. Asking for a model the source lacks raises
    ``RuntimeError``; the Copernicus sources are DSMs only.
source_collection_choice : str, optional
    ``gb_sct_lidar`` only: ``latest`` (default) uses the newest collection
    with tiles in the area (a warning names older ones that also cover it);
    a collection label (``phase-1`` ... ``phase-6``,
    ``national-lidar-programme``) uses that one. Collections are never mixed.
max_output_pixels : int, optional
    Largest output grid (cells) allowed, checked before any download; for
    the WCS sources the native cells requested are counted too.
max_download_megabytes : float, optional
    Largest download allowed (MB): an estimate checked before the fetch,
    and a running count that stops the transfer where lsdtt3 does the HTTP.
max_tiles : int, optional
    Largest number of tiles, source files or service requests allowed.
request_delay_milliseconds : int, optional
    Pause between requests to tile services (ms).

Returns
-------
Raster
    A projected raster of elevation (m): UTM (or ``target_epsg``), or the
    oblique frame. Network, GDAL, and invalid-request failures (including
    an area outside the source's coverage or over a size limit) raise
    ``RuntimeError``; an inconsistent combination of arguments raises
    ``ValueError``.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

signatures.definition: def fetch_dem(west: float = \0, south: float = \1, east: float = \2, north: float = \3, source: str = \4, target_epsg: int = \5, grid_spacing: float | None = \6, resampling: str = \7, nodata_value: float = \8, size_pixels: int = \9, cache_dir: str = \10, ot_dem_type: str = \11, pc_collection: str = \12, pc_asset: str = \13, http_timeout_seconds: int = \14, http_connect_timeout_seconds: int = \15, http_max_retry: int = \16, frame: object | None = \17, fetch_from_linear_feature: bool = \18, fetch_feature_fname: str = \19, fetch_feature_layer: str = \20, linear_feature_fetch_width: float = \21, linear_feature_fetch_end_buffer: float = \22, rotate_after_fetch: bool = \23, source_resolution_metres: float = \24, surface_model_choice: str = \25, source_collection_choice: str = \26, max_output_pixels: int = \27, max_download_megabytes: float = \28, max_tiles: int = \29, request_delay_milliseconds: int = \30) -> lsdtt3.Raster

exports.name: fetch_dem_for_outlets
exports.doc:
Fetch one or more in-memory DEMs around WGS84 outlet points.

The initial radius around each point is converted to WGS84 bounds, nearby
outlets are grouped, and large groups are split before each group is fetched.
The input GeoDataFrame is reprojected to WGS84 internally. Each group is
verified with D8 basin delineation, expanded if a basin reaches an edge or
nodata, and optionally refetched to its tight basin envelope.

Parameters
----------
outlets : geopandas.GeoDataFrame
    Point geometries defining outlet locations, in any declared CRS.
source : {"cop30_aws", "opentopography", "planetary_computer"}, optional
    DEM source, as in ``fetch_dem``. The national and polar sources are
    refused here, as in ``lsdtt-fetch-raster`` outlets mode: find the groups
    with ``cop30_aws``, then ``fetch_dem`` each group's area.
target_epsg : int, optional
    Output EPSG code; 0 selects UTM from each group's centre.
grid_spacing : float, optional
    Output cell size in target CRS units (m for UTM).
initial_radius_km : float, optional
    Initial half-width (km) of the box around each outlet before grouping.
auto_split_disconnected_basins : bool, optional
    Split groups whose outlets form separate clusters.
split_cluster_gap_km : float, optional
    Gap (km) between outlet clusters above which a group is split.
max_final_dem_area_km2 : float, optional
    Largest allowed grouped initial extent (km^2) before splitting it.
split_overlap_km : float, optional
    Overlap (km) between split extents.
max_basins_per_dem : int, optional
    Largest number of outlets per DEM; 0 means no limit.
cache_dir : str, optional
    Persistent download cache directory; empty means none.
resampling : str, optional
    GDAL warp resampling method.
nodata_value : float, optional
    Nodata value of the output DEMs.
snapping_method : {"none", "expanding_square", "downstream", "largest_area"}, optional
    Outlet snapping used before each basin delineation; the same rules as
    ``FlowInfo.snap_points`` and the CLI ``basin_outlet_snapping_method``.
contributing_pixels_threshold : int, optional
    Channel threshold (contributing pixels) that outlets are snapped to.
edge_buffer_pixels, nodata_buffer_pixels : int, optional
    Required basin clearance (pixels) from the DEM edge and invalid cells.
tight_bbox_buffer_pixels : int, optional
    Margin (pixels) added around the verified basins for the tight refetch.
verify_expand_factor : float, optional
    Factor (> 1) by which an extent grows when a basin reaches its edge.
verify_max_iters : int, optional
    Largest number of fetch-and-verify attempts per group.
tight_bbox_refetch : bool, optional
    Refetch a smaller final DEM around the verified basin footprint.
min_search_radius_pixels : int, optional
    Smallest expanding-square snap radius (pixels).
max_search_radius_pixels : int, optional
    Largest expanding-square snap radius when ``snapping_method`` is
    ``"expanding_square"``, and the half-width of the square searched for
    ``"largest_area"``.
mask_outside_basins : bool, optional
    Set cells outside the selected basin union to nodata in returned DEMs.
max_output_pixels, max_download_megabytes, max_tiles, request_delay_milliseconds
    Size limits and request pacing for each group's fetch, as in
    ``fetch_dem``.

Returns
-------
OutletFetchResult
    Grouped raster collection and copied outlet/group diagnostic tables.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

exports.name: fill_depth
exports.doc:
Return the non-negative elevation added by pit filling.

Parameters
----------
raster : Raster
    Elevation raster (m).
min_slope : float, default=0.0001
    Gradient (m/m) imposed across filled flats: each filled pixel is raised
    at least ``min_slope * cell_size`` (``* sqrt(2)`` on a diagonal step)
    above the pixel it drains to, so every pixel has a downhill route. 0
    fills to a flat surface.
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.

Returns
-------
Raster
    ``fill_pits(raster) - raster`` in metres (0 outside depressions).

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

exports.name: fill_hydraulic_surface
exports.doc:
Priority-flood a hydraulic ``z + h`` surface towards selected outlets.

The node-state raster uses 0 for excluded cells, 1 for active cells, and 3
for outlets. Unlike terrain pit filling, excluded/nodata cells are walls, not
drains. Code-3 cells are prescribed sinks wherever they occur.

Parameters
----------
surface : Raster
    Water-surface (or bed) elevation (m) to fill.
node_state : Raster
    Same grid: 0 excluded, 1 active, 3 outlet.
boundary_conditions : str, default='nnnn'
    Four NESW codes ``o``, ``n`` or ``p`` (periodic edges wrap).
slope_epsilon : float, default=1e-8
    Small gradient (m/m) imposed across filled flats so they drain.
check_valid_outlet : bool, default=True
    Require an outlet (code 3) in every connected active region.
priority_flood_backend : {"binary", "radix"}, default="binary"
    Priority-queue implementation; both give the same result.

Returns
-------
HydraulicSurfaceFill
    Filled surface, added depth (m) and added volume (m^3).

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

exports.name: fill_interior_nodata
exports.doc:
Fill nodata regions that are not connected to the raster edge.

Holes enclosed by valid pixels are filled by interpolation; nodata regions
that touch the raster edge are left as nodata.

Parameters
----------
raster : Raster
    Input raster.
method : {"laplacian", "iterative"}, default="laplacian"
    ``"laplacian"`` solves Laplace's equation across each hole (smooth
    surface through its rim); ``"iterative"`` repeatedly averages valid
    neighbours.
max_iter : int, default=10000
    Maximum number of iterations (positive).
tolerance : float, default=1e-6
    Convergence tolerance on the change per iteration, in raster units
    (positive).
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.

Returns
-------
Raster
    New in-memory raster.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

exports.name: fill_pits
exports.doc:
Fill depressions while imposing an optional minimum drainage slope.

Priority-Flood filling (Barnes et al. 2014): every pit and closed depression
is raised to its spill level, so all water can drain to the raster edge or
to nodata. The raster edge and pixels next to nodata act as outlets. Use the
result to build a ``FlowInfo``.

----------
raster : Raster
    Elevation raster (m).
min_slope : float, default=0.0001
    Gradient (m/m) imposed across filled flats: each filled pixel is raised
    at least ``min_slope * cell_size`` (``* sqrt(2)`` on a diagonal step)
    above the pixel it drains to, so every pixel has a downhill route. 0
    fills to a flat surface.
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.
priority_flood_backend : {"binary", "radix"}, default="binary"
    Priority-queue implementation: ``"binary"`` heap or ``"radix"``
    (hybrid radix heap). Both give the same result; only speed differs.

Raster

exports.name: fill_pits_boundary_aware
exports.doc:
Fill pits with NESW open, closed, periodic, or base-level boundaries.

Closed (``n``) edges are not outlets; periodic (``p``) edges wrap, so
depressions spilling across the seam are filled to their true spill level.
Fill with the same ``boundary_conditions`` you will give ``FlowInfo``.

Every valid pixel touching nodata is also an outlet, including one on a
closed edge, so DEMs with a nodata frame or voids (such as those from
``fetch_dem``) drain out where the data ends. Nodata pixels on an open edge
are skipped. Without a closed edge this is the same fill as ``fill_pits``.

    Elevation raster (m).

    ``make_boundary_conditions``). Both axes cannot be periodic; with a
    periodic axis the other edges must be open.
min_slope : float, default=0.0001
    Gradient (m/m) imposed across filled flats: each filled pixel is raised
    at least ``min_slope * cell_size`` (``* sqrt(2)`` on a diagonal step)
    above the pixel it drains to, so every pixel has a downhill route. 0
    fills to a flat surface.
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.
priority_flood_backend : {"binary", "radix"}, default="binary"
    Priority-queue implementation: ``"binary"`` heap or ``"radix"``
    (hybrid radix heap). Both give the same result; only speed differs.

Returns

Raster
    Filled DEM (m).

exports.name: find_channel_candidates
exports.doc:
Find multiscale channel-bottom candidates and return score and diagnostics.

Curvature is computed at ``n_scales`` polyfit scales between
``lambda_min_metres`` and ``lambda_max_metres``; pixels whose curvature
persists across adjacent scales, that are lower than their surroundings
and (optionally) line-like are scored as channel bottoms.

Parameters
----------
raster : Raster
    Elevation raster (m), typically a high-resolution lidar DEM.
lambda_min_metres, lambda_max_metres : float, default=3.0, 20.0
    Smallest and largest polyfit length scale (m).
n_scales : int, default=5
    Number of scales between them.
curvature_metric : str, default="plan_curvature"
    ``"plan_curvature"``, ``"tangential_curvature"``,
    ``"profile_curvature"``, ``"mean_curvature"``, ``"laplacian"``,
    ``"maximum_curvature"`` or ``"minimum_curvature"``.
positive_curvature_is_good : bool, default=True
    Treat positive curvature as channel-like (False inverts the sign).
depth_window_radius_metres : float, default=12.0
    Radius (m) of the window whose mean elevation minus the pixel's gives
    the local depth signal.
depth_window_shape : {"circular", "square"}, default="circular"
    Shape of that window.
weight_persistent, weight_depth, weight_slope : float, default=0.7, 0.3, 0.0
    Weights of the scale-persistence, depth and slope signals in the score.
score_threshold : float, default=0.5
    Score at or above which a pixel enters ``mask``.
use_hessian_filter : bool, default=True
    Also require line-like (elongated) curvature.
hessian_elongation_threshold : float, default=0.6
    Minimum Hessian elongation (0-1) when the filter is on.
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.

Returns
-------
ChannelCandidatesResult

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

exports.name: find_drains
exports.doc:
Find narrow drainage ditches from Frangi and curvature evidence.

Frangi valley enhancement is thresholded, small or blob-like components are
removed, and pixels with strong accumulation curvature (natural channels)
or a wide Frangi scale are masked out.

Parameters
----------
raster : Raster
    Elevation raster (m), usually a high-resolution lidar DEM.
sigma_min_metres, sigma_max_metres : float, default=1.0, 5.0

n_scales : int, default=4
    Number of Frangi scales.

    Frangi response at or above which a pixel is a candidate.
min_component_pixels : int, default=6
    Smallest connected component kept (pixels).
min_major_axis_pixels : float, default=5.0
    Smallest component major-axis length kept (pixels).
min_elongation : float, default=3.0
    Smallest component elongation (major / minor axis) kept.
accumulation_curvature_lambda : float, default=4.0
    Polyfit length scale (m) for accumulation curvature.
max_log10_abs_accumulation_curvature : float, default=-5.0
    Candidates whose blurred log10 |accumulation curvature| (1/m^2) exceeds
    this are removed.
max_frangi_scale_metres : float, default=1.8
    Candidates whose best Frangi scale (m) exceeds this are removed.

exports.name: find_flat_surfaces
exports.doc:
Detect and label flat surfaces from texture and local relief.

Each enabled roughness metric is computed in a moving window and thresholded
at a percentile of its own distribution (low roughness = flat); the metric
masks are combined, local relief must also be below
``max_relief_metres``, and connected flats are labelled.

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Elevation raster (m).
use_madk2 : bool, default=True
    Use MADk2 roughness (median absolute deviation of second differences;
    insensitive to uniform slope).
madk2_window_radius_metres : float, default=100.0
    MADk2 window radius (m).
madk2_threshold_percentile : float, default=25.0
    Pixels below this percentile of MADk2 count as flat.
use_residual_iqr : bool, default=True
    Use the interquartile range of residuals to a smooth reference surface.
iqr_method : {"fftw_highpass", "wavelet_quadratic", "moving_window_mean"}, default="fftw_highpass"
    How the reference surface is removed (the first two need FFTW).
iqr_fit_lambda_metres : float, default=500.0
    Reference-surface wavelength (m) for ``fftw_highpass`` and
    ``wavelet_quadratic``.
iqr_detrend_radius_metres : float, default=500.0
    Moving-window radius (m) for ``moving_window_mean``.
iqr_window_radius_metres : float, default=50.0
    Radius (m) of the window in which the IQR is computed.
iqr_window_shape : {"circular", "square"}, default="circular"
    Shape of that window.
iqr_threshold_percentile : float, default=25.0
    Pixels below this percentile of the IQR count as flat.
use_nvd : bool, default=False
    Use normal-vector dispersion (needs FFTW).
nvd_polyfit_lambda : float, default=10.0
    Wavelength (m) of the surface fit giving the normals.
nvd_window_radius_metres : float, default=100.0
    NVD window radius (m).
nvd_window_shape : {"circular", "square"}, default="circular"
    NVD window shape.
nvd_threshold_percentile : float, default=25.0
    Pixels below this percentile of NVD count as flat.
require_all_metrics_pass : bool, default=True
    True: a pixel must pass every enabled metric (AND); False: any (OR).
directional_close_line_length_pixels : int, default=0
    Length (pixels) of the line used to close small gaps in narrow non-flat
    corridors (channels, scarps) before labelling; below 3 disables it.
directional_close_n_angles : int, default=18
    Number of line orientations tried (18 = 10-degree steps).
min_component_pixels : int, default=100
    Smallest labelled flat (pixels).
relief_window_radius_metres : float, default=0.0
    Radius (m) of the square local-relief window, converted to the nearest
    whole number of cells (at least one); a radius of r cells is a
    (2r + 1)-cell side. 0 means 2 cells (a 5 x 5 window). Replaces the
    deprecated ``relief_window_side_pixels`` (a full side in cells).
max_relief_metres : float, default=1.0
    Pixels with local relief (max - min, m) at or above this are not flat.
    Replaces the deprecated ``relief_threshold_metres``.
remove_risers : bool, default=False
    Fit a plane to each flat and remove pixels with high residual relief
    (risers between terrace levels), then relabel.
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.

Returns
-------
FlatSurfaceResult
    Roughness rasters, per-metric and combined masks, and labelled flats.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

exports.name: find_perimeter_sources
exports.doc:
Find channel sources where valley floors cross the DEM perimeter.

lsdtt-channel-extraction ``run_perimeter_sources``; each keyword is that
CLI's ``perimeter_*`` parameter without the prefix (``n_outlets`` is
``n_perimeter_outlets``). For a floodplain that crosses the edge of the
DEM, the channel enters from outside, so no head exists inside the DEM.
The perimeter is traced, gentle wide low runs are found, and each is kept
as a source when the path inward from it is gentle and drains to one of
the ``n_outlets`` largest outlets.

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    The DEM after nodata handling: its mask is the valid region, and its
    elevations give the profile and gradients.
routed_dem : Raster
    The filled / flat-resolved DEM ``flow`` was built on.
flow : FlowInfo
    D8 routing on ``routed_dem`` with open boundaries on every edge
    (``boundary_conditions="oooo"``).
n_outlets : int, default=1
    Number of outer outlets (largest summed drainage area) sources must
    drain to.
min_valley_width_metres : float, default=300.0
    Narrowest gentle run (m) that counts as a valley-floor crossing.
max_gradient : float, default=0.05
    Largest perimeter gradient (m/m) that counts as gentle.
gradient_radius_metres : float, default=-1.0
    Plane-fit radius (m) of the perimeter gradient; negative is
    max(5 cells, 10 m).
gap_closing_metres : float, default=-1.0
    Steep gaps up to this length (m) inside a gentle run are absorbed;
    negative is max(2 cells, 20 m), 0 turns it off.
min_relief_metres : float, default=5.0
    Rise (m) needed on both sides for a run to be a low spot.
inward_check_distance_metres : float, default=500.0
    Length (m) of the path inward that is checked.
inward_max_gradient : float, default=0.10
    Steepest windowed gradient (m/m) allowed on that path.
inward_gradient_window_metres : float, default=-1.0
    Window (m) of that gradient; negative is max(5 cells, 25 m).
min_source_path_metres : float, default=-1.0
    Shortest path to the outlet (m) a source may have; negative is twice
    ``min_valley_width_metres``.
trim_pixels : int, default=0
    Erode the valid region by this many cells before tracing, moving the
    trace off interpolated edge values; trimmed cells still route flow.

Returns
-------
PerimeterSources

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

exports.name: find_risers
exports.doc:
Find risers: short steep steps between gentler surfaces, as open line segments.

lsdtt-feature-finder ``feature_type: find_risers``; each keyword is that
CLI's ``riser_*`` parameter without the prefix. A break-of-slope edge field
is adaptively thresholded and thinned, optionally gap-closed, split at
junctions into segments, and each segment gets a step height
``|2 dz(d) - dz(2d)|`` across it (0 on a planar slope, H across a step of
height H between treads of equal tilt). Segments below
``min_step_height_metres`` or ``min_segment_pixels`` are dropped. Risers
rarely close, so the product is segments, not polygons.

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Elevation (m).
search_mask : Raster or None, default=None
    Cells (> 0.5) where risers are looked for, for example a valley mask;
    None searches every valid cell.
edge_metric : {"vertical_excess_curvature", "curvedness", "maximum_curvature", "multidirectional_hillshade"}, default="vertical_excess_curvature"
    Edge field the lines are drawn on. The first three come from the
    polyfit; ``multidirectional_hillshade`` is the negated mean hillshade
    over ``multidirectional_hillshade_n_directions`` azimuths.
multidirectional_hillshade_n_directions : int, default=8
    Azimuths for ``multidirectional_hillshade``.
polyfit_lambda_metres : float, default=100.0
    Polyfit window (m) of the curvature metrics; also sets the default step
    window.
vec_adaptive_method : {"mean_std", "mean", "gaussian"}, default="mean_std"
    Adaptive threshold of the edge field.
vec_adaptive_std_factor : float, default=0.5
    ``mean_std``: local standard deviations above the local mean.
vec_adaptive_block_size_pixels : int, default=51
    Adaptive window side (odd, >= 3): wider than a riser, narrower than the
    spacing between risers.
vec_adaptive_C : float, default=0.0
    ``mean`` / ``gaussian``: offset below the local mean.
vec_adaptive_gaussian_sigma : float, default=0.0
    ``mean`` / ``gaussian``: pre-blur sigma; 0 means none.
closing_radius_metres : float, default=0.0
    Closing radius (m) of the binary mask before thinning; 0 means none.
binary_min_component_pixels : int, default=1
    Smallest binary component kept before thinning.
max_spur_pixels, max_terminal_loop_pixels : int, default=10
    Longest spur and terminal loop pruned from the skeleton.
min_component_pixels : int, default=1
    Smallest skeleton component kept.
gap_closing_algorithm_choice : {"none", "astar"}, default="none"

exports.name: identify_mountain_front
exports.doc:
Identify elevated terrain above a fitted low-ground piedmont surface.

Low ground (the piedmont) is found where local relief is small, a surface
is fitted to it, and pixels standing high above that surface are mountain.

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Elevation raster (m).

    Multi-scale low-ground criteria: a pixel is low ground when its local
    relief within ``radius_metres`` is below ``max_relief_metres``. Empty
    uses ``[[500, 50], [2000, 200]]``.
require_all_scales_pass : bool, default=False
    Require every scale to pass (True) or only the largest (False).
relief_window_shape : {"square", "circular"}, default="square"
    Shape of the relief windows.
use_elevation_filter : bool, default=False
    Also exclude pixels above an elevation percentile from low ground.

    That percentile, as a fraction (0-1).

    Method used to fit the low-ground surface.
ransac_inlier_tolerance : float, default=20.0
    ``plane_ransac``: largest residual (m) of an inlier.
ransac_max_iterations : int, default=1000
    ``plane_ransac``: number of iterations.
ransac_seed : int, default=1
    ``plane_ransac``: random seed.
spectral_lambda_metres : float, default=5000.0

    width.
residual_percentile : float, default=0.80
    Residual percentile above which pixels are classified as mountain
    (0.8 = the top 20% of residuals).
min_component_pixels : int, default=0
    Remove mountain components smaller than this (pixels); 0 skips.
infill_valley_radius_metres : float, default=0.0
    Radius (m) of a closing that seals valley notches in the mountain mask;
    0 skips.
return_diagnostics : bool, default=False
    Keep the per-scale local-relief rasters (``relief_rasters``).

    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.

    Low-ground mask, fitted surface, residual, mountain mask, and optional
    local-relief diagnostics.

exports.name: polyfit_metrics
exports.doc:
Compute several quadratic-fit surface metrics in one shared fit.

A quadratic surface ``z = a x^2 + b y^2 + c x y + d x + e y + f`` is fitted
in a square window around every pixel and the metrics are derived from its
coefficients (Florinsky 2017 names). x is east and y is north. Pixels whose
window is incomplete (near edges or nodata) are nodata.

Valid metric names and units:

- ``"fitted_surface"``: fitted elevation (m)
- ``"dzdx"``, ``"dzdy"``: gradient components east and north (m/m)
- ``"d2zdx2"``, ``"d2zdxdy"``, ``"d2zdy2"``: second derivatives (1/m)
- ``"slope"``: gradient magnitude ``sqrt(dzdx**2 + dzdy**2)`` (m/m)
- ``"slope_degrees"``: the same slope as an angle (degrees)
- ``"aspect_degrees"``, ``"aspect_radians"``: downslope direction,
  clockwise from grid north (true north with
  ``bearings_relative_to_true_north``)
- ``"laplacian"``: ``d2zdx2 + d2zdy2`` (1/m)
- ``"hessian_determinant"`` (1/m^2)
- ``"mean_curvature"`` (1/m), ``"gaussian_curvature"`` (1/m^2)
- ``"maximum_curvature"``, ``"minimum_curvature"``: principal curvatures
  k_max and k_min (1/m)
- ``"curvedness"`` (1/m), ``"shape_index"`` (dimensionless)
- ``"profile_curvature"`` (vertical, k_v), ``"plan_curvature"``,
  ``"tangential_curvature"`` (horizontal, k_h) (1/m)
- ``"difference_curvature"`` (0.5 (k_v - k_h)),
  ``"horizontal_excess_curvature"`` (k_h - k_min),
  ``"vertical_excess_curvature"`` (k_v - k_min) (1/m)
- ``"accumulation_curvature"`` (k_h k_v), ``"ring_curvature"`` (1/m^2)
- ``"rotor"`` (1/m)

Parameters
----------
raster : Raster
    Input elevation raster (m) in a projected metre CRS.
metrics : list[str]
    Requested metric names from the list above; an unknown name raises
    ``ValueError``.
lambda_metres : float, default=0
    Fitting length scale in metres, roughly the window width: the window
    is ``2W + 1`` pixels square with ``W = max(1, round(lambda_metres /
    (2 * cell_size)))``. Zero uses ``3 * cell_size``. Larger values smooth
    more. Must not be less than the cell size.
z_factor : float, default=1
    Elevation scale factor applied before metric calculation (for example
    0.3048 for elevations in feet).
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; zero selects the runtime default.
flat_slope_tolerance : float, default=1e-12
    Where the fitted gradient (m/m) is below this, the pixel is treated as
    too flat for direction-dependent metrics (aspect, plan, tangential and
    profile curvature, rotor).
bearings_relative_to_true_north : bool, default=False
    False: clockwise from grid north (grid up), so in an oblique frame
    (``RotationFrame``) 90 means along the feature. True: converted to
    true north with the grid convergence at each pixel (aspect metrics only; ``dzdx`` and ``dzdy`` stay grid
    components), as the CLIs'
    ``bearings_relative_to_true_north``; needs a raster with a CRS.

Returns
-------
dict[str, Raster]
    One newly allocated raster for every requested metric, keyed by name.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

signatures.definition: def polyfit_metrics(raster: lsdtt3.Raster, metrics: collections.abc.Sequence[str], lambda_metres: float = \0, z_factor: float = \1, n_threads: int = \2, flat_slope_tolerance: float = \3, bearings_relative_to_true_north: bool = \4) -> dict

exports.name: run_graphflood
exports.doc:
Run stationary graph-based hydraulic routing on an evolving ``z + h`` surface.

GraphFlood-style solver (Gailleton et al. 2024): rain falls on every active
cell, discharge is routed downslope over the water surface ``z + h`` (bed
plus water depth) and the depth ``h`` is updated each step until inflow and
outflow balance. Water leaves the domain ONLY through cells marked 3 in
``node_state``, whatever the edge codes in ``boundary_conditions``; to
drain across all four raster edges, mark them as outlets::

    edges = lsdtt3.make_outlet_mask(bed, True, True, True, True).to_numpy()
    node_state = lsdtt3.Raster.from_numpy(1 + 2 * edges, bed.mask_numpy(),
                                          bed.metadata)

With ``check_valid_outlet=True`` (the default) every connected group of
active cells must contain a code-3 cell, otherwise ``ValueError`` is raised.

Parameters
----------
bed : Raster
    Bed (terrain) elevation (m) in a projected metre CRS.
node_state : Raster
    Same grid as ``bed``: 0 excluded (wall), 1 active, 3 outlet (water
    leaving here is removed). Nodata pixels are excluded.
rainfall_rate : Raster
    Same grid: rainfall (effective runoff) rate in m/s, for example
    ``10 mm/h = 10 / 1000 / 3600 = 2.78e-6`` m/s.
friction_coefficient : Raster
    Same grid: coefficient ``K`` of the flow law ``q = K * h**a * S**b``
    (``q`` discharge per unit width, m^2/s). For Manning, ``K = 1 / n``
    (n in s m^(-1/3), for example n = 0.033 gives K = 30).
method : {"mfd", "dinf"}, default="mfd"
    Routing over the water surface: multiple-flow-direction or D-infinity.
boundary_conditions : str, default='oooo'
    Four NESW codes ``o``, ``n`` or ``p`` setting the neighbour topology of
    the edges (``p`` wraps to the opposite edge and must be paired). Edges
    do not drain by themselves: see ``node_state``.
mfd_exponent : float, default=1.0
    Exponent on slope used to split MFD discharge among receivers
    (positive).
condition_bed : {"none", "fill"}, default="none"
    ``"fill"`` priority-floods the bed towards the code-3 cells before
    routing.
fill_slope_epsilon : float, default=1e-8
    Small gradient (m/m) imposed across flats when the water surface (or
    bed) is priority-flooded towards the outlets.
check_valid_outlet : bool, default=True
    Require an outlet (code 3) in every connected active region.
friction_depth_exponent : float, default=5/3
    Exponent ``a`` on depth in the flow law (5/3 for Manning).
friction_slope_exponent : float, default=0.5
    Exponent ``b`` on hydraulic slope in the flow law (1/2 for Manning).
dt : float, default=0.001
    Time step in seconds of the depth update.
min_slope : float, default=0.0001
    Floor (m/m) on the hydraulic slope used in the flow law, so flat water
    surfaces still discharge.
point_inflows : array-like of float or None, default=None
    N x 3 array of ``(row, col, discharge_m3_s)``: extra inflow (m^3/s)
    added at given pixels, for example a river entering the domain.
max_steps : int, default=100
    Maximum number of time steps.
run_until_converged : bool, default=True
    Stop early when converged; if False run exactly ``max_steps`` steps.
convergence_check_every : int, default=10
    Check convergence every this many steps (positive).
median_dhw_convergence_tolerance_metres : float, default=1e-6
    Converged when the median absolute depth change per step (m) is at most
    this ...
median_dhw_relative_convergence_tolerance : float, default=0.0001
    ... and the median relative depth change is at most this.
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.
initial_water_depth : Raster or None, default=None
    Starting water depth (m) on the bed grid; None starts dry.

Returns
-------
HydraulicResult
    Water depth (m), water surface, discharges and convergence state.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

signatures.definition: def run_graphflood(bed: lsdtt3.Raster, node_state: lsdtt3.Raster, rainfall_rate: lsdtt3.Raster, friction_coefficient: lsdtt3.Raster, method: str = \0, boundary_conditions: str = \1, mfd_exponent: float = \2, condition_bed: str = \3, fill_slope_epsilon: float = \4, check_valid_outlet: bool = \5, friction_depth_exponent: float = \6, friction_slope_exponent: float = \7, dt: float = \8, min_slope: float = \9, point_inflows: object | None = \10, max_steps: int = \11, run_until_converged: bool = \12, convergence_check_every: int = \13, median_dhw_convergence_tolerance_metres: float = \14, median_dhw_relative_convergence_tolerance: float = \15, n_threads: int = \16, initial_water_depth: object | None = \17) -> lsdtt3.HydraulicResult

exports.name: run_graphflood_optimised_v2
exports.doc:
Run GraphFlood with the incremental v2 CPU kernels.

V2 uses a monotone radix heap in Priority-Flood, a bounds-free interior MFD
loop, specialised Manning exponents, and exact dirty-tile topology validation.
It falls back to a full Priority-Flood whenever a checked edge invalidates the
cached order. ``full_validation_every=0`` disables periodic full audits.
``node_state=2`` is a flux-only ghost cell: it routes its fixed
``prescribed_qin`` downslope while its depth and capacity-limited ``qout``
evolve normally. ``prescribed_qin=None`` means zero at ghost cells.

Parameters
----------
bed : Raster
    Bed (terrain) elevation (m) in a projected metre CRS.
node_state : Raster
    Same grid as ``bed``: 0 excluded (wall), 1 active, 3 outlet (water
    leaving here is removed). Nodata pixels are excluded.
rainfall_rate : Raster
    Same grid: rainfall (effective runoff) rate in m/s, for example
    ``10 mm/h = 10 / 1000 / 3600 = 2.78e-6`` m/s.
friction_coefficient : Raster
    Same grid: coefficient ``K`` of the flow law ``q = K * h**a * S**b``
    (``q`` discharge per unit width, m^2/s). For Manning, ``K = 1 / n``
    (n in s m^(-1/3), for example n = 0.033 gives K = 30).
boundary_conditions : str, default='oooo'
    Four NESW codes ``o``, ``n`` or ``p`` setting the neighbour topology of
    the edges (``p`` wraps to the opposite edge and must be paired). Edges
    do not drain by themselves: see ``node_state``.

    Exponent on slope used to split MFD discharge among receivers
    (positive).
condition_bed : {"none", "fill"}, default="none"
    ``"fill"`` priority-floods the bed towards the code-3 cells before
    routing.
fill_slope_epsilon : float, default=1e-8
    Small gradient (m/m) imposed across flats when the water surface (or
    bed) is priority-flooded towards the outlets.
check_valid_outlet : bool, default=True
    Require an outlet (code 3) in every connected active region.
friction_depth_exponent : float, default=5/3
    Exponent ``a`` on depth in the flow law (5/3 for Manning).
friction_slope_exponent : float, default=0.5
    Exponent ``b`` on hydraulic slope in the flow law (1/2 for Manning).
dt : float, default=0.001
    Time step in seconds of the depth update.
min_slope : float, default=0.0001
    Floor (m/m) on the hydraulic slope used in the flow law, so flat water
    surfaces still discharge.
point_inflows : array-like of float or None, default=None
    N x 3 array of ``(row, col, discharge_m3_s)``: extra inflow (m^3/s)
    added at given pixels, for example a river entering the domain.
max_steps : int, default=100
    Maximum number of time steps.
run_until_converged : bool, default=True
    Stop early when converged; if False run exactly ``max_steps`` steps.
convergence_check_every : int, default=10
    Check convergence every this many steps (positive).
median_dhw_convergence_tolerance_metres : float, default=1e-6
    Converged when the median absolute depth change per step (m) is at most
    this ...
median_dhw_relative_convergence_tolerance : float, default=0.0001
    ... and the median relative depth change is at most this.
reuse_topology : bool, default=True
    Reuse the cached routing order between steps when it is still valid.
dirty_tile_size : int, default=64
    Side (pixels) of the tiles whose routing is re-checked after a change.
full_validation_every : int, default=128
    Run a full topology audit every this many steps; 0 disables it.
initial_water_depth : Raster or None, default=None
    Starting water depth (m) on the bed grid; None starts dry.
prescribed_qin : Raster or None, default=None
    Fixed inflow discharge (m^3/s) of ``node_state`` 2 ghost cells; None
    means zero.

    Water depth (m), discharges, convergence state and timing counters.

exports.name: run_landslide_series
exports.doc:
Run a reproducible, annealing-aware landslide time series.

Provide exactly one budget: a fixed ``target_volume_per_event_m3`` or a
``long_term_erosion_rate_mm_kyr`` over the eligible host area. The final DEM
accumulates scars; the accompanying failure/depth rasters retain the latest
event at every pixel and can feed the cosmogenic functions directly.

Parameters
----------
dem : Raster
    Depression-conditioned elevation raster.
flow : FlowInfo
    Same-grid D8 routing topology.
start_time_yr, end_time_yr : float
    Inclusive simulation time interval in years.
mean_recurrence_yr : float
    Mean separation of events in years.
poisson_timing : bool
    Draw exponential waiting times when True; otherwise use fixed recurrence.
target_volume_per_event_m3, long_term_erosion_rate_mm_kyr : float
    Provide exactly one event-budget mode.
channel_threshold_pixels : int
    Channel threshold (contributing pixels) used by scar placement.
size_model : {"inverse_gamma", "truncated_pareto"}
    Landslide area distribution.
area_volume_preset : str
    Area-volume scaling preset: ``"larsen_global"``, ``"larsen_soil_scar"``,
    ``"larsen_bedrock_scar"``, ``"larsen_soil_all"``,
    ``"larsen_bedrock_all"``, ``"hovius_slab"`` or ``"hovius_parabolic"``.
min_pixels : int
    Smallest scar (pixels).
max_area_m2 : float
    Largest scar area (m^2); 0 means no cap.
anneal_time_yr : float
    Years before failed ground can fail again.
event_budget_relative_tolerance : float
    Relative tolerance of each event's volume against its budget.
budget_max_iter : int
    Largest number of budget-solver iterations per event.
seed : int
    Random seed.
active_mask : Raster, optional
    0/1 raster of pixels allowed to fail; None allows every pixel.

Returns
-------
LandslideSeriesResult
    Final terrain and scar rasters, timing, volume/rate closure, and event
    diagnostics.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

exports.name: sediment_connectivity_index
exports.doc:
Compute sediment connectivity using D8 topology; drainage area may be D8, MFD, or D-infinity.

Cavalli et al. (2013) index ``IC = log10(D_up / D_down)`` with
``D_up = mean(W) * mean(S) * sqrt(A)`` over the upslope area and
``D_down`` the sum of ``d / (W S)`` along the D8 path to the nearest sink;
``W = max(1 - R / R_max, 0.001)`` from the roughness R.

Parameters
----------
flow : FlowInfo
    D8 flow topology.
roughness : Raster
    Surface roughness on the flow grid (for example a local standard
    deviation of residual elevation, m).
slope : Raster
    Gradient (m/m); values below 0.001 are clipped in ``D_down``.
drainage_area : Raster
    Drainage area (m^2) from any routing scheme.
area_threshold_m2 : float
    Pixels with at least this drainage area (m^2) are sinks (channels).

Returns
-------
ConnectivityResult
    ``index``, ``weight`` (W), ``upstream`` (D_up) and ``downstream``
    (D_down) Rasters.

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton

exports.name: select_threshold
exports.doc:
Pick a threshold from a sample, as lsdtt-fluvial-surfaces picks its floodplain bounds.

The routine behind ``floodplain_threshold_algorithm_choice`` (and the
``qq_upper_departure`` floodplain second pass).

Parameters
----------
values : Raster or array-like of float
    The sample; for a Raster, its valid cells. Non-finite values are dropped.
threshold_algorithm_choice : {"fixed", "qq_gaussian", "cdf_divergence", "qq_upper_departure"}, default="qq_gaussian"
    ``qq_gaussian`` is Clubb et al. (2017): the lowest value at which the
    quantile-quantile plot rejoins a Gaussian drawn through two percentiles
    and stays on it. ``cdf_divergence`` fits a family of distributions and
    takes the value where the empirical CDF most exceeds the best fit.
    ``qq_upper_departure`` mirrors ``qq_gaussian`` for the upper tail.
    ``fixed`` returns ``fixed_value``.
fixed_value : float, default=0.0
    The threshold for ``fixed``.
qq_lower_percentile, qq_upper_percentile : float, default=25.0, 75.0
    Percentiles the Gaussian reference line is drawn through.
qq_threshold_fraction : float, default=0.01
    Fraction of the data range within which a quantile counts as on the line.

Returns
-------
dict
    ``threshold``, ``found`` (False when no threshold could be chosen, and
    ``threshold`` is then meaningless), ``n_values``, and for
    ``cdf_divergence`` ``best_family``, ``threshold_percentile`` and
    ``max_cdf_divergence``.

-------
B. Gailleton

    ``circular``: an elliptical dome in the middle; ``arc``: mountains
    against one edge with a front that curves into the piedmont.
edge : {"north", "south", "east", "west"}, default="north"
    Edge the mountains are against (``halfspace`` and ``arc`` only).
ridge_elevation : float, default=2000.0
    Crest elevation (m).
piedmont_elevation : float, default=0.0
    Base (piedmont) elevation (m).
front_fraction : float, default=0.2
    Size of the mountain zone as a fraction of the grid extent: the ridge
    half-width (``linear``), the ellipse semi-axes (``circular``) or the
    front's distance from the edge (``halfspace``, ``arc``).
noise_amplitude : float, default=100.0
    Amplitude (m) of the fractal noise added to the surface.
seed : int, default=1
    Random seed.
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.

Returns
-------
dict
    ``"elevation"`` (Raster, m) and ``"mountain_mask"`` (Raster, 1 =
    mountain, 0 = piedmont).

-------
B. Gailleton

exports.name: synthetic_network
exports.doc:
Optimise a synthetic D8 optimal channel network and derive its chi steady-state DEM.

An optimal channel network (OCN) is found by simulated annealing of the
energy ``sum(A**gamma * L)`` over D8 networks, and a steady-state
stream-power DEM is built on it from chi.

Parameters
----------
metadata : RasterMeta
    Output grid.
outlet_mode : {"single_south", "all_coast", "north_south"}, default="single_south"
    One outlet at the centre of the south edge; every edge pixel an outlet;
    or outlets along the north and south edges.
periodic_columns : bool, default=False
    Wrap the grid east-west (route the DEM with ``p`` on east and west).
outlet_spacing : int, default=1
    ``"north_south"`` only: column spacing of the outlets (larger values
    force wider basins).
gamma : float, default=0.5
    Energy exponent on drainage area.
n_iterations : int, default=-1
    Annealing iterations; <= 0 uses 40 x n_rows x n_cols.
temperature_scale : float, default=1.0
    Multiplier on the annealing temperature schedule.
m_exponent, n_exponent : float, default=0.45, 1.0
    Stream-power exponents used to build the DEM from chi.
relief_metres : float, default=1000.0
    Relief (m) of the output DEM.
seed : int, default=1
    Random seed.

Returns
-------
SyntheticNetworkResult

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd

exports.name: wiener_filter
exports.doc:
Attenuate high-frequency white noise with an adaptive Wiener filter.

A power law fitted to the spectrum between the two signal wavelengths gives
the signal; the noise level comes from the near-Nyquist spectrum; each
frequency is weighted by signal / (signal + noise).

Parameters
----------
raster : Raster
    Elevation raster (m) in a projected metre CRS.
signal_wavelength_long_metres : float, default=1000.0
    Longest wavelength (m) of the band used to fit the signal.
signal_wavelength_short_metres : float, default=100.0
    Shortest wavelength (m) of that band.
window : {"hann", "hamming", "none"}, default="hann"
    Taper applied before the FFT.
clip_to_valid_rectangle : bool, default=False
    First crop to the largest all-valid rectangle (the result is then
    smaller than the input).
n_threads : int, default=0
    OpenMP thread count; 0 uses the runtime default.

Returns
-------
Raster
    Filtered DEM (m).

Authors
-------
B. Gailleton
S. M. Mudd
